vision.title: The Tail Thing

inputs.title: The Tail Thing
inputs.logline: When small squirrel Bo cannot get himself out the door for his first visit to the Learning Circle, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very tail he wants to hide may be the thing that helps him belong.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen stages a tiny, over-careful honey heist in the golden meadow, but every crunch and Fuzzby’s sleeping presence turns the sneaking into comic suspense. The beat is about Keen wanting the prize without being seen, while the world makes invisibility impossible.
beats.want: Keen wants to reach the honeycomb without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that being clever and quiet is not the same as being ready for what the world does back.
beats.kidRead: A funny sneaking game where every little sound could wake the bee.
beats.adultRead: A child trying to control every variable, unaware that bodies and worlds never behave perfectly.
beats.emotionalIntent: Playful tension: giggles held in the body, with the audience leaning toward the honeycomb.

Fuzzby's eyes POP open. Beat.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen

beats.storyBeat: A drifting speck of pollen lands on Keen’s nose and turns his careful plan into a losing battle with his own sneeze. The turn is the sneeze that wakes Fuzzby and exposes Keen completely.
beats.want: Keen wants to hold the sneeze in long enough to stay hidden.
beats.need: He needs to accept that his own body can reveal him, and that being caught is survivable.
beats.kidRead: The sneeze is coming, coming, coming — then it explodes.
beats.adultRead: The harder he suppresses the truth, the bigger the reveal becomes.
beats.emotionalIntent: Escalating comic pressure followed by a bright release.

beats.storyBeat: Fuzzby half-wakes just long enough to deliver territorial grandeur over the honeycomb, then immediately falls back asleep. Keen receives the impossible-sounding barrier with wounded curiosity rather than defeat.
beats.want: Fuzzby wants to defend the honeycomb without actually waking up properly; Keen wants to understand whether the refusal is absolute.
beats.need: Fuzzby needs his importance witnessed even in sleep; Keen needs to feel the sting of a closed door before he can later help Bo face one.
beats.kidRead: The bee makes a huge sleepy warning and then snores again.
beats.adultRead: Fuzzby’s bluster is all status, while Keen’s tiny question makes the rejection feel child-sized and real.
beats.emotionalIntent: Warm comic rejection with a little poke of disappointment underneath.

beats.storyBeat: Keen walks away from the failed honeycomb attempt and lands beside Zenny’s untouched stillness. Her meditation hum turns the scene from busy sneaking into a dry, calm comic button.
beats.want: Keen wants to leave with dignity; Zenny wants to remain undisturbed.
beats.need: Keen needs a quiet witness to his small defeat; Zenny’s stillness lets the comedy breathe instead of pushing another gag.
beats.kidRead: Keen gives up and the calm bee is just sitting there going ommm.
beats.adultRead: The scene releases the failed scheme by cutting from effort to acceptance, without anyone explaining the feeling.
beats.emotionalIntent: A soft deadpan exhale after sneeze chaos.

orderedEvents.text: Soft mist floats through tall trees. AIDA sits beside a crystal bowl. She slowly circles a mallet around the rim. A warm tone hums through the clearing. Her ROSE QUARTZ PENDANT begins to glow. Pink light fills her eyes.
VISION – THROUGH AIDA'S EYES
A small red squirrel sits inside a hollow tree. He packs a satchel. Unpacks it. Packs it again. He doesn't move. BACK TO SCENE. Aida gently stops the bowl. She places a paw on her heart.

beats.storyBeat: Aida’s still bowl ritual opens a rose-lit vision of Bo in his hollow tree, endlessly packing and unpacking but not moving. The supernatural moment is quiet and domestic, showing need before anyone names it.
beats.want: Aida wants to listen through the bowl and understand who needs help.
beats.need: She needs to trust the small signal and respond without controlling the outcome.
beats.kidRead: A magic pink vision shows a squirrel stuck with his bag.
beats.adultRead: The child’s repeated packing reads as the familiar loop before a hard first step.
beats.emotionalIntent: Mysterious tenderness, held in stillness and rose light.

orderedEvents.text: Warm sunlight fills a cozy hollow tree. BO, a young red squirrel, sits beside a small satchel. Next to him lies a shiny CONKER. His Mum calls to him from offscreen, we never actually see his Mum.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo's Mum
orderedEvents.text: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
Bo calls back to his Mum

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: I’ll go in a minute Mum.
(to the conker) Or forty. Forty sounds much better to me.

beats.storyBeat: Inside the warm hollow tree, Bo delays leaving by answering his offscreen Mum and negotiating with his conker and satchel. The room is safe, but the door already feels far away.
beats.want: Bo wants a few more minutes before he has to go.
beats.need: He needs someone to notice that delaying is not laziness; it is his worry trying to keep him safe.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps trying to put off going and talks himself into a much longer wait.
beats.adultRead: The ordinary parent call from offscreen makes the first-day threshold feel painfully familiar.
beats.emotionalIntent: Cozy but trapped, with small comic denial protecting a real wobble.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: What if it’s not OK?!

beats.storyBeat: Bo reaches the open door and freezes, then retreats into a conker-in, conker-out loop that climbs from maybe-tomorrow to real panic. The conker becomes the physical switch for his uncertainty.
beats.want: Bo wants to decide whether today is safe enough to go.
beats.need: He needs permission to take a step without first making the day feel perfectly safe.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps putting the conker in and out because he can’t decide.
beats.adultRead: The satchel ritual is the child version of rehearsing every possible outcome and still not leaving.
beats.emotionalIntent: Comic repetition tightening into a sincere stuck feeling.

beats.storyBeat: Keen appears at the doorway with a friendly knock, startling Bo so hard the conker flies. Bo’s private loop is suddenly witnessed, but Keen’s entrance is gentle rather than invasive.
beats.want: Keen wants to introduce himself and begin Aida’s errand; Bo wants to recover control of the conker and the room.
beats.need: Bo needs a first witness who does not make the exposure worse.
beats.kidRead: Keen pops in, Bo jumps, and the conker goes everywhere.
beats.adultRead: The newcomer arrives at exactly the vulnerable moment, but his warmth keeps it from becoming humiliation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Startle comedy that lands safely instead of sharply.

beats.want: Bo wants his tail to behave normally before Keen judges him.
beats.need: He needs to experience the feared reveal being met with delight.
beats.kidRead: Bo’s tail poofs enormous and Keen thinks it is amazing.
beats.adultRead: A child’s most embarrassing tell becomes lovable because one person reacts generously first.
beats.emotionalIntent: The catch-and-release: exposure, then instant relief through Keen’s impressed face.

beats.storyBeat: Keen offers his own useless tail as a silly comparison, making himself the joke so Bo does not have to be. Bo’s tail softens, his smile grows, and the two leave together.
beats.want: Keen wants to make Bo feel safe enough to step outside; Bo wants the offer to feel small and possible.
beats.need: Bo needs companionship, not a fix, and Keen needs to practice courage as making room for someone else’s wobble.
beats.kidRead: Keen wiggles his tail and nothing happens, which is funny enough to help Bo smile.
beats.adultRead: Keen lowers the status gap by being ridiculous first; that is the kindness that unlocks the door.
beats.emotionalIntent: Warm, silly release into the first real step.

BO makes his tail do ‘The Thing’ on command. POOF!
BO/KEEN 3, 2, 1 …
POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again.

orderedEvents.text: 3,2,1 … POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again. Bo giggles.

beats.storyBeat: On the dappled forest path, Keen turns Bo’s tail thing into a countdown game. Bo can make the poof happen on purpose now, and the feared body response becomes shared play.
beats.want: Bo and Keen want to repeat the tail poof as a game while walking.
beats.need: Bo needs to feel agency over the thing that embarrassed him.
beats.kidRead: They count down and the tail goes poof again and again.
beats.adultRead: Play gives Bo a safe way to rehearse being seen before the real group sees him.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light, rhythmic joy with forward motion.

beats.want: Aida wants to join Bo without making herself too grand; Bo wants to know whether she is safe to trust.
beats.need: Bo needs the elder to come down to his level, leaves and all.
beats.kidRead: Aida gets caught by tricky trees and has a funny leaf on her ear.
beats.adultRead: Authority becomes safe because it arrives imperfect, then honours the effort already in Bo’s bag.
beats.emotionalIntent: Disarming warmth: the leader becomes a companion, not a judge.

beats.need: He needs to separate having the wobble from being unable to move.
beats.kidRead: Even Aida gets that feeling, and she still goes.
beats.adultRead: The elder’s admission lets courage be ordinary rather than heroic, which is what makes it reachable.
beats.emotionalIntent: The episode’s quiet centre: simple, grounded, and held a breath longer than expected.

orderedEvents.speaker: Sunny

direction.premise: Bo wants to make it to the Learning Circle without anyone noticing the big nervous thing his tail does; instead, being witnessed kindly turns the tail from a problem to a doorway into friendship.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo step toward a group who already know each other while letting the part of himself he wants to hide be seen?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is met with delight instead of judgement.
direction.externalJourney: Keen is pulled from a failed honey sneak to help Bo leave his hollow tree, walk through the Whispering Woods, arrive at the Learning Circle, share his tail trick with the group, and end the day with a new friend.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from postponing and repacking to taking one small step, then another, until his tail is no longer an alarm bell but a playful part of him he can offer to others.
direction.relationshipChanges: Keen shifts from mischievous solo adventurer to gentle witness and walking companion; Aida becomes the steady elder who normalises going while wobbly; the Learning Circle moves from imagined judgement to real delight; Fuzzby remains the comic mirror of failed sneaking, now turned back on himself.
direction.emotionalCurve: Playful sneakiness opens the episode, then Aida’s quiet vision redirects the story into Bo’s small domestic worry. The middle rises through stop-start panic, is softened by Keen’s admiration and Aida’s honesty, then glows into movement. The Learning Circle brings the feared exposure, but it lands as welcome. The final garden gag releases the episode with the honeycomb still untouched and friendship quietly proved.
direction.comedyCurve: Physical suspense in the honeycomb sneaking gives way to sneeze comedy, then to Bo’s conker-packing loop and tail poof escalation. Keen’s dead-still tail reverses the embarrassment into shared silliness. Sunny’s over-bright welcome and Luna’s tiny brake reset the group rhythm, and Fuzzby’s flower disguise pays off the opening honeycomb challenge with a self-inflicted crash.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s warning in Scene 1 return as the final garden button in Scene 8. Bo’s conker-packing loop sets up his stop-start threshold fear, which pays off in his first steps on the glowing path. The tail’s first unwanted poof becomes a chosen game in the woods, then a group celebration at the Learning Circle, then the shared drawing joke. Aida’s vision of Bo not moving pays off in Aida and Keen helping him move without forcing him.
direction.visualMotifs: Thresholds, satchel-in/satchel-out, the conker in Bo’s paws, Bo’s tail expanding and softening, leaves and forest paths, pink-and-blue light joining on the ground, and the honeycomb sitting untouched as a comic measuring stick of growth.
direction.sonicMotifs: Tiny crunches and pops begin as sneaky danger; Bo’s tail poofs become softer and more playful; Aida’s rose-quartz bowl tone opens the unseen need; Keen’s aquamarine note joins Aida’s warmth on the path; Zenny’s low meditation hum bookends the bee comedy.
direction.climax: On the forest path, Aida’s rose light and Keen’s blue light join, and Bo takes step after step with them, repeating Aida’s phrase back as an action rather than a lesson.
direction.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail does the thing in front of everyone and the group responds with curiosity and delight; later, Bo and Keen draw and laugh together while Aida watches from the edge, pendant glowing softly.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, lightly funny relief: the room should feel that Bo did not become a different squirrel; he became seen, and the honeycomb button lets the audience leave laughing without erasing the cost of the day.

storyTruth.emotionalFearOrWound: Bo fears being the unknown one among friends who already belong to each other.
storyTruth.transformedAction: Bo walks through the door, steps down the glowing path, and lets his tail poof in front of the group as something they can enjoy with him.
storyTruth.themeProvenThroughAction: The thing Bo hides becomes the thing he shares, and sharing it is what lets the group welcome him.

tapestryMap.physicalMotifArc: Hands hover over honey, satchel, conker and tail at first; by the middle, paws sit beside rather than grab; by the end, the tail moves freely and playfully in open space.
tapestryMap.visualMotifArc: Closed circles and thresholds dominate early: honeycomb, snore bubbles, hollow door, satchel mouth, conker. These open into the winding path, then into the Learning Circle, and finally a wide golden garden where the honeycomb remains untouched.
tapestryMap.colourAndLightJourney: Warm golden morning starts mischievous and safe; Aida’s scene adds rose mist and inner light; Bo’s hollow is warm but enclosed; the woods use dappled green-gold with worry sitting in shadow; the crystal path blends rose and azure; the Learning Circle is sunny and communal; the final garden settles into golden sunset.
tapestryMap.sourceSoundArc: Crunches, pops, sneezes and offscreen calls make the world startle the characters early. Mid-episode, footsteps and rustling leaves slow the pace. The climax lets crystal tones and path ambience take over. The ending returns to buzz-crash and meditation hum as comic release.
tapestryMap.musicMotifArc: Begin with plucky sneak pizzicato and tiny bee buzz rhythm, move into Aida’s low rose-quartz bowl tone, then a small squirrel motif around the conker. Keen’s B note and Aida’s G note join on the path, with a light circle-theme emerging once Bo is welcomed. The final cue pares down to a warm sunset button with bee comic accents.
tapestryMap.environmentalMetaphor: Homes, honeycombs and bags are safe containers; the path is the uncertain middle; the circle is the feared social world that proves soft; the garden ending shows the world unchanged, but Bo and Keen’s relationship has changed inside it.
tapestryMap.openingImage: Keen in golden dew tiptoeing toward an untouched honeycomb while Fuzzby sleeps directly on top of the prize.
tapestryMap.finalImage: A wide golden garden: the honeycomb still untouched, Fuzzby tangled in flower petals nearby, and the day’s warmth resting over a joke that no longer feels lonely.
tapestryMap.transformedMeaning: The same world that first popped, startled and blocked the characters becomes a place where surprises can be shared, witnessed and laughed with.

transformationMap.believes: Maybe the tail can be played with, but the Learning Circle is still the real unknown.
transformationMap.feels: Buoyant while the game works, then small again when the path ahead returns.
transformationMap.does: Bo poofs the tail on command, giggles, then stops and sits when the bigger social fear comes back.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Keen can accompany him, but cannot make the group less unknown; Bo needs an older truth from Aida.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: The lift drops into a quiet ache, because the joke did not magically remove the worry.

transformationMap.believes: Everyone there already belongs, and he does not.
transformationMap.feels: Still, tight, satchel-gripping, looking down the path from the outside.
transformationMap.does: Bo says the true problem aloud while Keen sits beside him and Aida sits with space, not pressure.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Aida joins as a grounded witness; the group is still offscreen and imagined, which makes it feel larger.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: A held breath: this is the one quiet centre where the child sees Bo stuck and the adult feels the old doorway fear.

transformationMap.believes: Going can happen even while the wobbly feeling comes too.
transformationMap.feels: Not fixed, but accompanied.
transformationMap.does: Bo accepts the offered paw-light, watches Aida and Keen let their crystals answer, and takes one step, then another, down the glowing path.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Bo is not carried or corrected; he is walked with, between rose confidence and blue courage.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Hopeful release: the path itself seems to say the next step is enough.

transformationMap.believes: The tail thing can be part of how others know and enjoy him.
transformationMap.feels: Open, delighted, still carrying a trace of the morning’s cost.
transformationMap.does: Bo lets the tail poof at the Learning Circle, draws the joke into Keen’s picture, and laughs with a friend while Aida watches from the edge.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Bo has moved from visitor to participant; Keen has become his friend; Aida’s role softens from guide to proud witness.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Belonging with a laugh still attached, not a clean reset.

tapestryMap.physicalMotifArc: Hands hover over honey, satchel, conker and tail at first; by the middle, paws sit beside rather than grab; by the end, the tail moves freely and playfully in open space.
tapestryMap.visualMotifArc: Closed circles and thresholds dominate early: honeycomb, snore bubbles, hollow door, satchel mouth, conker. These open into the winding path, then into the Learning Circle, and finally a wide golden garden where the honeycomb remains untouched.
tapestryMap.colourAndLightJourney: Warm golden morning starts mischievous and safe; Aida’s scene adds rose mist and inner light; Bo’s hollow is warm but enclosed; the woods use dappled green-gold with worry sitting in shadow; the crystal path blends rose and azure; the Learning Circle is sunny and communal; the final garden settles into golden sunset.
tapestryMap.sourceSoundArc: Crunches, pops, sneezes and offscreen calls make the world startle the characters early. Mid-episode, footsteps and rustling leaves slow the pace. The climax lets crystal tones and path ambience take over. The ending returns to buzz-crash and meditation hum as comic release.
tapestryMap.musicMotifArc: Begin with plucky sneak pizzicato and tiny bee buzz rhythm, move into Aida’s low rose-quartz bowl tone, then a small squirrel motif around the conker. Keen’s B note and Aida’s G note join on the path, with a light circle-theme emerging once Bo is welcomed. The final cue pares down to a warm sunset button with bee comic accents.
tapestryMap.environmentalMetaphor: Homes, honeycombs and bags are safe containers; the path is the uncertain middle; the circle is the feared social world that proves soft; the garden ending shows the world unchanged, but Bo and Keen’s relationship has changed inside it.
tapestryMap.openingImage: Keen in golden dew tiptoeing toward an untouched honeycomb while Fuzzby sleeps directly on top of the prize.
tapestryMap.finalImage: A wide golden garden: the honeycomb still untouched, Fuzzby tangled in flower petals nearby, and the day’s warmth resting over a joke that no longer feels lonely.
tapestryMap.transformedMeaning: The same world that first popped, startled and blocked the characters becomes a place where surprises can be shared, witnessed and laughed with.

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Keen tries to get honey; Aida senses Bo and redirects Keen toward helping him.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: Keen’s body betrays the sneak with pollen and sneezes; Aida’s vision reveals a child who cannot move forward.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Aida connects the comic sneeze outside her clearing to the real need inside Bo’s hollow.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Keen is summoned to go with Aida’s purpose behind him.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: Who is the squirrel in the vision, and why can’t he leave?

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Bo must leave home for the Learning Circle.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalStart: Warm domestic safety with a small trapped delay.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: The satchel, conker and open door become a loop that keeps Bo from leaving; Keen’s arrival exposes him.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Keen’s impressed response to the tail thing changes Bo’s feared exposure into a first moment of being liked.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Bo smiles and walks out with Keen.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: Can that tiny confidence survive the walk to the group?

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Keen, Bo and Aida need to keep moving toward the Learning Circle.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalStart: Playful recovery as Bo performs the tail poof on purpose.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: The sight of the path brings back the fear of entering a group who already knows each other.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Aida sits beside Bo, admits through action and simple presence that going can still happen every time, and joins her rose light with Keen’s blue light.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Bo takes steps down the glowing path with them.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: Will the group actually welcome the thing Bo feared?

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Bo meets the bears and finds his place in the Learning Circle.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalStart: Big welcoming energy that could overwhelm him.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: Sunny’s brightness, everyone watching, and Bo’s tail poof create the exact exposure he feared.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Misty and Amie respond with curiosity and delight, turning the tail into a shared game; later Bo and Keen draw and laugh as friends.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Aida watches Bo belong without needing to manage the moment.
sequenceBlueprint.dominantAudienceFeeling: Joyful acceptance, with the parent seeing how little it took: one kind reaction.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: How does the episode release the honeycomb setup and leave us laughing?

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Fuzzby tries to sneak his own honeycomb back while Keen gardens.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: Fuzzby’s flower disguise cannot overcome his own full-throttle clumsiness.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Keen effortlessly repeats Fuzzby’s opening warning back at him, and Zenny’s tiny smile lets affection leak through the deadpan.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Fuzzby is stuck in petals, Zenny returns to stillness, and the honeycomb remains untouched.
sequenceBlueprint.dominantAudienceFeeling: Clean laugh with a warm afterglow.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: None; the day rests on a joke that carries the relationship forward.

northStar.surfaceStory: Bo tries to delay leaving his hollow oak for the Learning Circle, gets caught in a conker-and-door panic loop, then Keen arrives, sees the feared tail “thing,” and helps Bo take one small step out for a walk.
northStar.universalTruth: Sometimes the part of yourself you are trying hardest to hide is the part someone kind sees first — and they do not flinch.
northStar.childClearWant: Bo wants to not go today because he is scared nobody will like him if his tail acts funny.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Bo needs one safe witness who reacts with delight instead of alarm, so leaving the room can feel possible without pretending the fear is gone.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If my tail does the thing where people can see it, I won’t belong.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Keen changes the room by being gently present rather than clever: he arrives at the doorway, does not laugh at Bo, looks at the tail with wonder, then makes his own tail the joke so Bo no longer has to be the joke.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A child can rehearse bravery alone forever; often the first real movement happens only when another person stands nearby and makes being seen feel less dangerous.
northStar.sceneTurn: The turn lands when Bo’s tail does exactly what he feared and Keen answers it with sincere awe — “Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING.” Bo’s shame does not disappear, but it loses enough grip for curiosity to enter.
audienceJourney: Safe, cosy delay: the child recognises the “one more minute” stall.
Comic worry: the conker loop makes panic playable and visible.
Startle: Keen’s knock exposes Bo’s private rehearsal.
Little gasp: the tail does the dreaded thing in front of someone new.
Relief-laugh: Keen’s useless-tail demonstration redirects embarrassment into shared silliness.
Forward warmth: leaving for a walk feels like a first step, not a solved problem.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: A small brave exhale: Bo is not ready for everything, but he is no longer alone inside the doorway.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any explanation of Bo’s fear or Keen’s kindness beyond the locked lines. The conker-in/conker-out loop, Bo’s retreat from the open door, the tail’s visible betrayal, Keen’s wonder-filled look, and the useless-tail demonstration should carry the meaning without extra dialogue.
northStar.environmentPressure: The hollow oak is warm and protective, but the open doorway, Mum’s offscreen call, the lunch satchel, outside daylight, and the visible path to the Learning Circle all press Bo toward leaving. The conker turns the room into a little decision machine: each roll toward or away from the door physically restarts the argument in Bo’s body.

transformation.entryBelief: If I wait a little longer and keep checking, I can avoid today and keep my tail from ruining things.
transformation.entryFeeling: Cosy but trapped; comfort is turning into panic because the safe room also proves he has not left.
transformation.pressureBehaviour: He answers Mum with delay, negotiates with the conker and satchel, reaches the door, freezes, retreats, and repeats the conker choice until the loop becomes panic.
transformation.costlyChoice: When Keen sees the tail do the thing, Bo does not slam the door or fully hide; he stays present long enough to hear Keen’s wonder and then accepts the walk.
transformation.exitBelief: Maybe being seen by one kind someone is survivable; maybe my tail is not only a problem.
transformation.exitAction: Bo leaves the hollow oak with Keen for fresh air, carrying the fear forward instead of resolving it inside the room.

tapestry.physicalMotif: The conker is Bo’s decision switch: in, out, in, out — a tiny object doing the work of a giant worry. The tail is the uncontrolled truth that interrupts the switch and forces the real fear into the room.
tapestry.sonicMotif: Keep the hollow quiet enough that small sounds feel huge: Mum’s offscreen call, satchel rustle, conker taps, the open-door hush, Keen’s gentle knock, then the soft comic beat of Keen demonstrating his tail doing nothing. Silence should widen just before and just after the tail ‘thing.’
tapestry.colourAndLightProgression: Begin in honeyed, enclosed warmth inside the hollow oak, with the doorway carrying brighter outside light that feels too big. As Keen enters, let the threshold light become less threatening and more shared; by the exit, the same daylight reads as fresh air rather than exposure.
tapestry.thematicVisualContrast: Private loop versus shared movement: Bo alone circling objects in a safe room, then Bo and Keen oriented toward the same doorway. Also controlled small conker versus uncontrollable large tail — the thing Bo can manage versus the thing he cannot.
tapestry.openingClosingRhyme: Opening image: Bo inside the hollow, clutching the mechanics of delay while the door waits. Closing image: Bo crossing toward that same door with Keen beside him. The doorway changes meaning from test to invitation, while the worry remains visible enough to preserve the episode’s larger journey.

inputs.title: The Tail Thing
inputs.logline: When small squirrel Bo cannot get himself out the door for his first visit to the Learning Circle, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very tail he wants to hide may be the thing that helps him belong.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen stages a tiny, over-careful honey heist in the golden meadow, but every crunch and Fuzzby’s sleeping presence turns the sneaking into comic suspense. The beat is about Keen wanting the prize without being seen, while the world makes invisibility impossible.
beats.want: Keen wants to reach the honeycomb without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that being clever and quiet is not the same as being ready for what the world does back.
beats.kidRead: A funny sneaking game where every little sound could wake the bee.
beats.adultRead: A child trying to control every variable, unaware that bodies and worlds never behave perfectly.
beats.emotionalIntent: Playful tension: giggles held in the body, with the audience leaning toward the honeycomb.

beats.need: She needs to trust the small signal and respond without controlling the outcome.
beats.kidRead: A magic pink vision shows a squirrel stuck with his bag.
beats.adultRead: The child’s repeated packing reads as the familiar loop before a hard first step.
beats.emotionalIntent: Mysterious tenderness, held in stillness and rose light.

beats.emotionalIntent: Cozy but trapped, with small comic denial protecting a real wobble.
