treatments.name: Treatment 1 — The Room That Keeps Saying “Not Yet”
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels like they are inside Bo’s private delay machine: cosy at first, then funnier and tighter as every object seems to vote on whether he leaves. Children read it as a suspenseful game of “will he go?” Adults recognise the exhausting ritual of rehearsing courage until rehearsal becomes the trap. Keen’s arrival should feel like a window opening, not a rescue squad entering.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Bo owns the scene until Keen reframes him. The camera’s sympathy stays with Bo’s Want — keep the day small, keep the tail unseen, keep the decision reversible — while quietly exposing his Need: one kind witness who does not treat the tail as a disaster. Keen is not staged as the solution; he is the first presence that makes staying visible survivable.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The governing mechanism is environmental participation: the conker, satchel, doorway light, Mum’s offscreen call and Bo’s tail all become players in his argument with today. The comedy escalates through overcommitment: Bo tries to make one tiny object decide a giant life question, and the more seriously he treats the conker, the more obvious his panic becomes. The dramatic turn is Keen’s sincere awe at the tail, which converts private shame into shared wonder without explaining it.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo’s acting is small-choice panic: paws hover, commit, retract; his attention ricochets from conker to satchel to open door to tail. His body keeps trying to be tidy while his tail tells the truth bigger than he can. He does not perform “fear” broadly; he performs control failing. Keen enters with gentle curiosity: he knocks like he knows a room can be startled, then keeps his body soft and available. When he demonstrates his own tail doing nothing, he makes himself the silly object on purpose — not clowning for attention, but offering Bo somewhere safe to laugh.
treatments.visualGrammar: The hollow oak begins as a warm circular enclosure, all curved surfaces and reachable objects, but the open door is a bright vertical interruption that feels too large for Bo’s current courage. Composition should make the room feel like it is looping: Bo repeatedly returns to the same decision objects, but each return is less cosy and more cornered. Once Keen appears, the visual grammar shifts from circles to shared lines toward the doorway. The door does not get brighter; Bo’s relationship to it changes.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like Bo’s worry: close to the objects he can control, hesitant near the threshold, easily startled by interruption. It may discover Keen only when Bo does, because the shock is part of Bo’s experience. After Keen’s wonder at the tail, the camera stops acting like a hiding place and becomes a witness that can hold both embarrassment and kindness in the same emotional space.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Before Keen, motion is repetitive and fussy: conker in, conker out, satchel touch, door approach, retreat. Stillness arrives only as freeze — the body trapped. Keen introduces a different stillness: calm attention. The tail’s sudden uncontrolled action is the biggest movement in the scene, and Keen’s still, delighted look is what changes its meaning. At the end, Bo and Keen’s shared movement out should be modest, not triumphant: one small walk, not a victory parade.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use depth as pressure. The foreground holds Bo’s manageable objects; the mid-ground holds Bo; the background doorway holds the day he is avoiding. Mum’s voice comes from beyond the room but never needs a body; the outside world is present as sound and light. When Keen arrives, he occupies the threshold without conquering it, turning the doorway from a boundary into a meeting place. The conker should travel through the room in a way that lets the audience always understand where the door is relative to Bo.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Start with soft domestic tempo, then let the conker loop create comic meter: decision, reversal, decision, reversal. Each spoken line from Bo should land as another attempt to negotiate with time, not as exposition. The panic peak is not loudness alone; it is the moment the loop can no longer contain the tail. Keen’s “Whoa” must slow the rhythm sharply — the scene inhales — then the useless-tail demonstration releases the tension quickly into a gentle laugh.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by decision changes, not coverage. Cut when the conker changes the argument, when the doorway becomes too big, when Keen’s presence changes the privacy of the room, and when Bo’s tail forces the real fear into view. Avoid automatic reaction cutting; sometimes the funniest or truest reaction is letting Bo and the object share the frame until the audience feels how seriously he is taking it. Hold briefly after Keen’s awe so Bo’s shame has time to become curiosity.
treatments.openingImage: Bo inside the hollow oak with the lunch satchel and conker close at hand, the open doorway waiting in brighter depth like a question he is trying not to answer.
treatments.closingImage: Bo and Keen moving toward the same doorway together, the conker left behind in the warm room, the outside light now reading as fresh air rather than exposure.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: I would challenge any version that simply plants the camera in a cosy room and watches Bo talk. The space must actively argue with him. We should not default to safe interior two-shots once Keen enters; the threshold is the emotional event, and the lens must make the audience feel the doorway change meaning.

treatments.name: Treatment 2 — The Tail Is the Truth-Teller
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience waits for the secret thing before they fully know what it is. The scene plays like a gentle comic mystery: Bo keeps organising the day around something unseen, and the room seems to hold its breath around his tail. Children anticipate the funny reveal; adults feel the ache of a child trying to edit out the part of himself that might be noticed first. The relief comes when Keen notices exactly that part and loves it first.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The scene belongs to Bo’s tail as the visible truth Bo cannot manage. Bo’s face and words insist on delay and control; the tail carries the Need by refusing to behave like a normal, hideable object. Keen’s point of view enters at the turn: he does not see a problem to fix, he sees something amazing. The emotional handoff is from Bo’s shame to Keen’s wonder, then back to Bo as he tests whether that wonder might be safe to believe.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The main mechanism is concealment to revelation. Bo tries to keep the feared “thing” offstage, verbally and physically, but the tail keeps becoming the scene’s loudest truth. The conker loop is the decoy game; the tail is the real engine. The comedy comes from Bo negotiating with the wrong object while the actual problem waits behind him, then announces itself at precisely the worst social moment.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo should behave as if his tail is a separate, embarrassing roommate. He angles around it, overcorrects, hushes it, pleads with it, and finally addresses it directly with “Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!” His embarrassment is active: he tries to fold himself smaller around something that will not be made small. Keen’s performance is radically uncomplicated. He does not scan Bo for weirdness; he receives the tail with open delight. His own useless-tail bit is deliberately underwhelming — the joke is how earnestly he presents nothing as a demonstration.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visual grammar keeps the tail partially withheld early, not by artificial coyness but by Bo’s own blocking and the hollow’s curves. The audience feels there is a large unspoken presence in the room before the full action declares itself. The door and conker are secondary visual motifs; the tail is the emotional weather. At the turn, the composition should allow the tail to dominate the space in a way Bo fears is humiliating, then let Keen’s gaze re-scale it from too much to wonderful.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is an uneasy confidant. It knows Bo is hiding something but does not expose him cruelly. It follows his attempts to manage the tail, then allows the tail to break the frame’s politeness when the “thing” happens. With Keen, the camera adopts honest discovery: not shock, not spectacle, but wonder. It must be close enough to Bo for the embarrassment to sting and open enough for Keen’s kindness to have room.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Bo’s small body tries stillness as self-protection, while the tail supplies involuntary movement. That contrast is the scene. The conker’s little taps are tiny controlled motion; the tail’s “thing” is uncontrolled truth. Keen’s entrance should be physically quiet so the tail remains the largest action. His own tail demonstration then becomes anti-motion: he invites a result, waits, and nothing happens. The nothing is the punchline and the act of generosity.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The hollow should frame the tail as something that cannot quite fit Bo’s preferred version of himself. Curved walls, low shelves, satchel, and doorway create gentle obstacles that make his attempts to hide legible without adding business. Depth is used less as outside pressure and more as concealment: the tail appears from behind Bo, furniture, or the doorway edge in ways that keep the geography clear but let the reveal build.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm is a slow reveal with nervous comic interruptions. Mum’s call starts the clock; Bo’s “in a minute” buys false calm. The conker loop accelerates just enough to distract us, then Keen’s knock punctures the private ritual. Bo’s fear line should run with more exposed urgency because he is no longer rehearsing alone. The tail action lands as the scene’s loudest silent confession. Keen’s “Whoa” creates the catch; “Mine does nothing. Watch.” creates the release.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should protect the reveal rather than chop the scene into conventional exchanges. We cut to change what the audience is allowed to know about the tail, or to register the altered meaning in Keen’s eyes. Avoid showing every stage of the tail too early. Once the tail is fully witnessed, let the scene breathe; cutting away too fast would imply the show is embarrassed by it too.
treatments.openingImage: A warm hollow interior where Bo appears busy with leaving-preparations, but the frame leaves a suspicious pocket of space near him that keeps drawing attention without explaining why.
treatments.closingImage: The once-feared tail still present as Bo agrees to fresh air, no longer hidden out of frame; Keen’s ordinary useless-tail joke has made room for Bo’s extraordinary one.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: I would push against making the tail reveal merely a big gag insert. If we photograph it like a punchline object, we betray Bo. The frame must first understand it as shame, then let Keen’s look transform it into wonder. The challenge is to make one physical feature carry suspense, comedy, and tenderness without exploiting it.

treatments.name: Treatment 3 — Threshold Duet: Inside Voice, Outside Friend
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience experiences the scene as a doorway duet. On one side is Bo’s warm, circular, rehearsed inside-world; on the other is daylight, Learning Circle, and being seen. Keen does not burst in and drag Bo out. He meets him exactly at the border, and the scene becomes about how two characters can stand near the same threshold until one small step becomes possible.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The governing point of view is the threshold itself: what does it feel like when leaving is not a location change but an exposure? Bo’s Want is to stay on the safe side of the line. His Need is to discover the line can be shared. Keen’s emotional role is to make the doorway feel inhabited by kindness rather than judgement. Bo remains the emotional owner; Keen is the relational shift.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The dramatic mechanism is status change of the doorway. At first the open door has power over Bo; he approaches it like a test he is failing. The conker loop turns the door into a comic referee: in means maybe, out means no, and Bo keeps appealing the call. Keen’s knock changes the door from threat to encounter. The tail “thing” is the dreaded exposure at the threshold; Keen’s awe reclassifies exposure as connection.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo should always know where the doorway is, even when looking away. His body orbits it: drawn forward, then flung inward by thought. He treats the conker like a legal ruling, then panics when the ruling changes too fast. When Keen appears, Bo’s first impulse is not rudeness but startled privacy — someone has stepped into the place where his rehearsed bravery was supposed to remain unseen. Keen remains careful at the border. He does not crowd Bo, and his friendliness is measured enough that Bo can keep listening. His tail demonstration is performed as a sincere comparison, not a slick joke.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene is built around crossing lines. The hollow interior has warm low light, tactile safety, and circular shapes; the doorway has vertical brightness and open air. Early frames keep Bo separated from that brightness by furniture, satchel, or his own retreating path. As the scene progresses, the threshold becomes more porous: Keen’s presence softens it, Bo’s tail accidentally crosses emotional boundaries before Bo does, and finally both characters orient outward together.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera begins inside with Bo, reluctant to go near the doorway unless he does. It retreats when he retreats and feels the open air as too much. Keen’s knock is not covered from a safe outside angle; it interrupts the inside pattern. After the turn, the camera can occupy the threshold itself, no longer belonging only to inside or outside. It becomes the shared space Bo has earned.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement is organised as approach and retreat. Bo’s steps toward the door carry preparation without completion; each retreat is faster and less dignified. Stillness at the doorway is the costly beat: he is not doing nothing, he is meeting the size of the day. Keen’s stillness is different — patient, inviting, non-demanding. The final movement out should preserve uncertainty in Bo’s body: a small exhale, a glance back perhaps, then continued forward motion with Keen beside him.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth tells the whole story. Interior foreground equals delay and objects; the threshold is mid-depth pressure; the path beyond is visible enough to be real but not overdefined. Do not make the outside a magical solution. It remains bright and big. The change is that Keen now shares the depth relationship with Bo. Mum’s offscreen voice and lunch satchel keep ordinary life present; this is a child going out for the day, not a grand quest departure.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm alternates between domestic call-and-response and physical hesitation. Mum’s line is the everyday bell; Bo’s answer buys time. The door approach slows the scene into suspended breath, then the conker loop restarts it with comic taps. Panic rises as the loop fails to produce certainty. Keen’s entrance is a soft rupture. The tail beat widens time, then Keen’s useless-tail demonstration lets the rhythm become walkable again.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are threshold-motivated: cut when Bo’s relation to the door changes, when the conker reverses his decision, when Keen changes the doorway from empty pressure to friendly presence, and when the tail makes the invisible fear visible. Resist symmetrical inside/outside coverage. The audience should not feel we are comparing two territories mechanically; they should feel one boundary slowly losing its power.
treatments.openingImage: The open doorway seen from within the warm hollow, with Bo held back among his leaving-things as if the room itself still has a paw on him.
treatments.closingImage: The same doorway now shared by Bo and Keen as they head out for fresh air, leaving the room warm behind them but no longer necessary as a hiding place.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: I would challenge any staging that treats Keen’s arrival as a simple entrance into a room. The doorway is the scene’s co-star. We need compositions that make the threshold emotionally alive without locking characters to permanent sides. The camera should be willing to live on the border once Bo can.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Treatment 1 — The Room That Keeps Saying “Not Yet,” strengthened by Treatment 2’s tail-as-truth emphasis and Treatment 3’s threshold logic
combinedFrom: Treatment 1 — The Room That Keeps Saying “Not Yet”
Treatment 2 — The Tail Is the Truth-Teller
Treatment 3 — Threshold Duet: Inside Voice, Outside Friend
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience is inside Bo’s private delay ritual as it turns from cosy play into a little panic machine, then feels the room open when Keen sees the feared tail and answers with wonder instead of alarm.
treatmentSelection.rationale:
Treatment 1 is the spine because it best serves the scene’s truth: Bo is not simply hiding a tail or refusing a doorway; he is using small controllable rituals to postpone being seen. That gives children a clear game — conker, satchel, door, repeat — while adults feel the ache of rehearsed bravery becoming its own trap. It also gives the scene active behaviour rather than explanation: objects argue with Bo, the doorway pressures him, the tail betrays the truth, and Keen changes the air by witnessing rather than fixing.

Treatment 2 contributes the necessary emotional sharpness: the tail must not become just a funny reveal. It is Bo’s visible Need, the part that refuses to obey his Want. Keen’s delight has to transform the tail from “too much” to “amazing” in Bo’s eyes for one fragile second. That is the gasp-and-release core of the scene.

Treatment 3 contributes the cleanest spatial meaning: the doorway changes status. It begins as exposure, becomes encounter when Keen arrives, then becomes shared movement. That gives the closing image emotional clarity without pretending Bo is cured.

The selected approach has the strongest character specificity: Bo controls, loops, negotiates, and shrinks; Keen arrives carefully, wonders sincerely, and makes himself gently ridiculous so Bo does not have to be the joke. It also has the best rhythm: domestic delay, comic loop, panic tightening, sudden exposure, charged pause, relief-laugh, small forward step. The scene will be memorable because a conker, a doorway, and a tail become the whole emotional argument without added explanation.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks:
No selected element may depend on fixed character lanes, keeping everyone visible, habitual action/reaction coverage, safe camera placement, repeated close-up punctuation, mechanical shot counts, generic “cinematic” language, or merely illustrating the script.

Treatment 1 passes as the governing treatment because it assigns the camera and room an experiential relationship to Bo’s worry rather than a coverage plan. Its warning against safe two-shots is correct and must hold.

Treatment 2 is not selected alone because, if overplayed, its concealment/reveal design could turn the tail into a mystery gag or punchline object. Any version that withholds the tail coyly, cuts to it as a comic insert, or photographs Keen’s reaction as ordinary surprise is rejected. The tail must be shame first, wonder second, never spectacle.

Treatment 3 is not selected alone because the doorway concept can become too schematic if it turns into inside/outside staging geometry. Any version that locks Bo and Keen to permanent sides of the frame, treats the threshold as a diagram, or compares territories through symmetrical coverage is rejected. The doorway matters only insofar as Bo’s body and Keen’s care change its meaning.

The combined selection must keep Bo as emotional owner, Keen as safe witness, the tail as visible truth, and the final exit as a small survivable step — not a solved-problem victory.

scene.purpose: Bo’s private delaying ritual turns from cosy control into exposed panic, then Keen’s gentle witnessing makes one small step toward the doorway possible.
scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo leave the hollow oak while the tail he wants hidden remains visible and uncontrolled?
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: Bo begins inside his safest space, with the Learning Circle already pressing from beyond the open doorway through light, sound, satchel and Mum’s offscreen call.
scene.handoverToNextScene: Bo and Keen leave the room together for fresh air; Bo’s worry is not solved, but being seen has become survivable enough to move.

beats.sourceScript: Inside the warm hollow tree, Bo delays leaving by answering his offscreen Mum and negotiating with his conker and satchel. The room is safe, but the door already feels far away.
exactDialogue: Bo's Mum: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
Bo: I’ll go in a minute Mum.

orderedEvents.text: Warm sunlight fills a cozy hollow tree. BO, a young red squirrel, sits beside a small satchel. Next to him lies a shiny CONKER. His Mum calls to him from offscreen, we never actually see his Mum.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo's Mum
orderedEvents.text: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
Bo calls back to his Mum

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: I’ll go in a minute Mum.
(to the conker) Or forty. Forty sounds much better to me.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo's Mum
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: I’ll go in a minute Mum.

beats.whatChanges: The room shifts from simple morning safety into a delaying chamber: Mum’s offscreen prompt makes the open doorway active, and Bo answers by keeping the decision reversible through the conker and satchel.
beats.whoDrives: Bo drives the delay; Mum’s voice supplies the pressure from outside the hollow.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits to see whether Bo will actually pick up the lunch satchel and leave, while noticing that he is already treating the door as too large a step.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo stays close to manageable objects, answers Mum with a promised delay, and keeps the conker and satchel as things he can touch instead of crossing the threshold.
beats.consequence: The day has officially begun, but Bo has not moved toward it; the cosy hollow starts to feel like a loop rather than a refuge.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The beat hands into the conker decision-game: Bo has bought one minute, and the audience is primed to watch that minute stretch into a comic trap.

emotionContract.entryState: Comforted by the warm hollow and the nearby lunch satchel and conker.
emotionContract.pressure: Mum’s offscreen call, the Learning Circle, the lunch reminder and the open doorway all ask for forward motion now.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo chooses delay instead of departure, keeping the decision small enough to handle by touching objects in the room.
emotionContract.exitState: Still safe, but more trapped; the room now contains proof that he has not gone.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: His attention ricochets between conker, satchel and door; his paws hover and retract before his line promises only a minute.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience understands that the minute is not just a minute; the doorway is the real problem.

comedyContract.setup: Mum asks from outside that it is time to go and reminds him about lunch.
comedyContract.expectation: Bo will collect the satchel and leave.
comedyContract.disruption: Bo treats the nearby objects as if they can negotiate the morning for him.
comedyContract.button: His line makes delay sound tiny even as the room shows the size of what he is avoiding.
comedyContract.hold: Let the satchel, conker and open doorway share the emotional space long enough for the audience to feel how seriously Bo is outsourcing the decision.

beats.sourceScript: Bo reaches the open door and freezes, then retreats into a conker-in, conker-out loop that climbs from maybe-tomorrow to real panic. The conker becomes the physical switch for his uncertainty.
exactDialogue: Bo: Maybe, I’ll go tomorrow instead. Tomorrow sounds much better than today. Tomorrow everything will OK, not today.
Bo: Today could be OK.
Bo: What if it’s not OK?!

orderedEvents.text: He places the conker in the bag and walks towards the front door but just as he opens the door Bo freezes in place. Panic sets in.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: Maybe, I’ll go tomorrow instead. Tomorrow sounds much better than today. Tomorrow everything will OK, not today.
Bo scurries back inside and takes the Conker out of his bag. Bo realizes he must go – today.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: Today could be OK.
He sighs deeply and then puts the Conker back in the bag again. But his anxiety starts to rise again.
But, Today might not be OK.
Bo pulls the Conker out of the bag -again - and holds it in his hands. Panic really kicks in.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: What if it’s not OK?!

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: Maybe, I’ll go tomorrow instead. Tomorrow sounds much better than today. Tomorrow everything will OK, not today.

beats.whatChanges: Bo’s delay becomes a visible panic loop: the door freezes him, and the conker-in/conker-out ritual starts deciding today, tomorrow and disaster for him.
beats.whoDrives: Bo drives the loop by repeatedly assigning the conker authority over his decision.
beats.audienceAnticipation: Children anticipate the conker’s next verdict; adults anticipate the moment the ritual will stop helping and start tightening around him.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo approaches the open door, freezes, retreats, then repeatedly moves the conker in and out while arguing aloud between tomorrow, today and not-OK.
beats.consequence: The conker’s tiny movement takes on giant stakes, and Bo’s body becomes less tidy with each reversal until panic breaks through the game.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The comedy of the decision switch hands into vulnerability: the room’s playful loop has made Bo easier to startle and more exposed.

emotionContract.entryState: Trying to make leaving feel manageable by reducing it to one object and one doorway.
emotionContract.pressure: The open door confronts him with the outside day, and each conker choice fails to settle the fear.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo chooses to keep restarting the decision instead of accepting any one answer.
emotionContract.exitState: Cornered by his own ritual; the panic is now louder than the cosy delay.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He freezes at the threshold, retreats, repeats the conker action, and his final line breaks the earlier negotiation rhythm.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds both the laugh of the conker loop and the ache that Bo cannot get out by deciding harder.

comedyContract.setup: Bo uses a conker as the physical switch for whether today can happen.
comedyContract.expectation: One clear conker choice will settle the argument and let him move.
comedyContract.disruption: Every choice creates the opposite choice; the more seriously Bo obeys the conker, the less control he has.
comedyContract.hold: Hold the final conker position with Bo’s panic still attached to it so the audience catches the absurd size of the job he has given the object.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: The conker, Bo’s paws, the lunch satchel and the open doorway remain readable in relation to one another so the audience tracks the decision loop and the pressure of the exit.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Each conker move has small tactile weight: paw pads gather it, set it down or pull it back; the satchel shifts only when Bo actually touches or bumps it, proving the room is responding to his fussy momentum.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A repeated in-out pattern tightens into faster, less tidy reversals until Bo’s body freezes and the final line pops out as the ritual fails him.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the conker into a magical chooser or animated character.
Do not make the loop so fast that the audience loses where the doorway is.
Do not cut away from the conker’s final position before Bo’s panic lands.

beats.sourceScript: Keen appears at the doorway with a friendly knock, startling Bo so hard the conker flies. Bo’s private loop is suddenly witnessed, but Keen’s entrance is gentle rather than invasive.
exactDialogue: Keen: 11	Hi! I'm Keen.
Keen: Aida sent me. She thought we should meet.

orderedEvents.text: A shadow appears at the doorway. Keen appears at the open door and gently taps on the hollow tree. Shave and a Haircut knock. He peeks inside.
Beat.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: 11	Hi! I'm Keen.
Bo jumps. The conker flies into the air. He catches it, fumbles it several times and finally hugs it. BO looks from the Conker to KEEN immediately

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: Aida sent me. She thought we should meet.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Keen
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: Aida sent me. She thought we should meet.

beats.whatChanges: Bo’s private ritual becomes shared space: Keen appears at the doorway and the conker flies, exposing the loop without punishing Bo for it.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives the change by entering gently at the threshold; Bo’s startled body supplies the consequence.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits to learn whether this new witness will make the room more dangerous or less dangerous for Bo.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen knocks and introduces himself from the doorway instead of barging in; Bo startles hard enough to launch the conker out of its decision role.
beats.consequence: The conker is no longer in control, and Bo can no longer pretend the delay ritual is private.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The startle laugh hands into social exposure: Bo must now speak the real fear to someone who is present.

emotionContract.entryState: Overwound inside the conker loop, focused on controlling the next tiny decision.
emotionContract.pressure: A new bear appears exactly where the day has been pressing in: the open doorway.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo does not shut the encounter down immediately; despite the startle, he remains in the room with Keen present.
emotionContract.exitState: Exposed and startled, but not invaded; Keen’s softness keeps the threshold from becoming an attack.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: The conker flies from Bo’s startle, while Keen stays at the doorway with simple, friendly lines rather than pushing deeper into the room.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds the relief that Keen is gentle and the tension that Bo’s real fear is about to surface.

comedyContract.setup: Bo’s whole body is locked into the conker’s private decision ritual.
comedyContract.expectation: The next movement will be another controlled conker choice.
comedyContract.disruption: A friendly knock turns control into a startled launch.
comedyContract.button: Keen’s calm introduction lands against Bo’s oversized startle.
comedyContract.hold: Keep a brief beat on the contrast between the flown conker and Keen’s soft doorway presence so the laugh does not make Keen feel careless.

beats.sourceScript: Bo blurts the social fear and his tail immediately does the very thing he dreads. Keen looks at the giant tail with wonder, reframing Bo’s embarrassment before Bo can disappear into it.
exactDialogue: Bo: What if nobody likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?
Bo: Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!
Keen: 14	Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING.
Bo: 15	…you think so?

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: What if nobody likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?
His tail suddenly POOFS twice its size. Bo grabs it.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!
The tail refuses. POOFS twice its size again.
Keen stares. Impressed.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: 14	Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING.
Bo pauses his struggle with his tail and begins to calm down.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: 15	…you think so?

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: What if nobody likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!

beats.whatChanges: The real fear becomes visible: Bo names the worry that nobody will like him, the tail does the thing, and Keen’s wonder changes the tail from disaster to amazement for one fragile moment.
beats.whoDrives: Bo drives the exposure by blurting the fear; the tail forces the truth into view; Keen drives the emotional turn by answering with awe.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience inhales, waiting to see whether Keen will flinch, laugh at Bo, or make the feared tail feel unsafe.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo asks the tail to be normal when it acts out; Keen stays present, looks with delighted sincerity and names the tail as amazing.
beats.consequence: Bo does not disappear into shame; his question back to Keen shows curiosity entering the space where panic had been.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The gasp of exposure hands into a gentle opening: Bo is still embarrassed, but Keen’s response gives him enough safety to listen.

emotionContract.entryState: Socially exposed and trying to explain why the Learning Circle feels impossible.
emotionContract.pressure: His feared tail behaviour happens immediately in front of the new witness.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo stays present long enough to hear Keen’s wonder instead of fully hiding or ending the encounter.
emotionContract.exitState: Unsure but newly curious; the tail may not only be a problem if someone can see it with delight.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: Bo blurts the fear, pleads with his tail, then softens into the small, disbelieving question after Keen’s line.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: Keen’s awe remains in the room as a new possible meaning for the tail, but Bo’s fear is still visible.

comedyContract.setup: Bo fears his tail will do the thing where others can see it.
comedyContract.expectation: The tail’s action will confirm disaster and make Bo the joke.
comedyContract.disruption: The tail does act out, but Keen receives it as amazing rather than ridiculous.
comedyContract.hold: Hold briefly after Keen’s awe so Bo’s shame has time to become curiosity; do not rush into the next gag.

beats.sourceScript: Keen offers his own useless tail as a silly comparison, making himself the joke so Bo does not have to be. Bo’s tail softens, his smile grows, and the two leave together.
exactDialogue: Keen: 16	Mine does nothing. Watch.
Keen: 17	See? Nothing.
Keen: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
Bo: That does sound nice.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: 16	Mine does nothing. Watch.
Keen turns around and wiggles. His tail hangs there. Completely still.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: 17	See? Nothing.
Bo looks at Keen's tail. Then at his own. His tail slowly deflates. He almost smiles.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
BO’s smile grows to a full smile.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: That does sound nice.
His tail deflates, picks up his bag and walks out the door with Keen.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Keen
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.

beats.whatChanges: Keen turns himself into the safe silly object, Bo’s tail softens, and the doorway becomes a shared path rather than a test.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives the release by demonstrating his own tail doing nothing and offering a walk; Bo drives the final change by accepting the step.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits for Bo to either retreat back into the room or accept Keen’s low-pressure invitation toward the outside.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen shows his tail’s uselessness without demanding Bo change, then suggests fresh air; Bo lets the smile grow and agrees.
beats.consequence: Bo and Keen move toward the doorway together, leaving the conker behind in the warm room as the decision machine loses its job.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The relief-laugh hands to forward warmth: Bo is not cured, but he is no longer alone at the threshold.

emotionContract.entryState: Fragile curiosity after Keen’s awe, still carrying embarrassment and uncertainty.
emotionContract.pressure: The doorway and Learning Circle remain ahead, and Bo must choose whether to stay inside or move with Keen.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo accepts a small walk as the next step, not as a promise that everything is fixed.
emotionContract.exitState: Warmer and braver by one notch; fear travels with him, but so does a kind witness.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: His tail softens, his smile grows, and he answers Keen’s invitation before moving toward the same doorway with him.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The conker remains behind as a trace of the old loop, while Bo carries a small brave exhale into the next scene.

comedyContract.mechanism: Hiding failure turned into generous self-joke
comedyContract.setup: Bo’s tail has just been treated as amazing, but Bo is still unsure what to do with being seen.
comedyContract.expectation: Keen might explain, reassure too much, or make Bo’s tail the continued focus.
comedyContract.disruption: Keen makes his own tail the intentionally useless comparison, moving the joke onto himself.
comedyContract.hold: Let Bo register that Keen is offering silliness, not judgement, before the invitation to walk redirects the scene toward the doorway.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn the hollow oak from cosy safety into the first little delaying chamber.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Mum’s offscreen call activates the open doorway, and Bo answers by staying with the conker and satchel instead of moving toward the threshold.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The room stops being only comforting; Bo’s promised minute reveals itself as a way to keep the decision reversible.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin embedded with Bo’s controllable objects, then let the bright doorway sit in depth as a pressure he keeps not choosing.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo remains inside beside the satchel and conker, with the open doorway visibly waiting beyond him.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Put the audience inside Bo’s private delay ritual before the room tightens.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: Low, close interior view across the conker and lunch satchel toward Bo, with the open doorway held farther back as a bright vertical interruption.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: Mum calls from outside; Bo looks between the objects and the door, answers, “I’ll go in a minute Mum,” then quietly extends the delay by treating the conker as his listener.
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: Small-choice panic: paws hover near the satchel, attention flicks to the doorway, then returns to the conker for safety.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: Bo still inside the hollow with the conker and satchel close, the doorway unanswered in the background.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: No internal cut; the one idea is the room becoming Bo’s delay machine.

shots.purpose: Establish Bo’s Want as delay and the room’s pressure as active without explaining the fear yet.
shots.audienceExperience: Cosy recognition with a small adult wince: the child sees a familiar morning stall, while adults recognise rehearsal replacing action.
shots.openingImage: Bo inside the hollow oak beside the lunch satchel and conker, with the open doorway brighter behind him like an unanswered question.
shots.principalPerformance: Bo keeps the body tidy and small; every attempt to answer the day sends his paws back to the objects he can control.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera stays close to Bo’s worry and lets the doorway press from depth rather than announcing the space from safety.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: Mum’s call makes the day official, but Bo converts it into a negotiable pause.
shots.closingImage: Bo remains beside the conker and satchel while the open doorway holds its place in the room.
shots.transitionReason: A cut is stronger than remaining continuous because the next unit begins a new causal engine: Bo physically tests the doorway and the conker loop starts making decisions for him. Holding one flow would blur the shift from cosy delay to repeated panic ritual.
shots.providerBoundaryExplanation: This unit’s natural 15 seconds plus the next unit’s natural 25 seconds would exceed the 30-second provider limit, and the next unit needs a fresh opening anchor at the threshold where the panic loop begins.

cinematographyContract.storyPointOfView: Bo’s private delay ritual, with the world outside present only as voice and doorway pressure.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceStart: Near and protective, sharing the scale of the objects Bo trusts.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceEnd: Still near, but with the doorway feeling larger because he has not crossed it.
cinematographyContract.revealStrategy: Reveal the problem indirectly: the door is visible before Bo admits anything is wrong.
cinematographyContract.shotScale: Intimate interior object-led medium-close scale, not a room master.
cinematographyContract.lensIntent: A close, child-height relationship that makes the conker and satchel feel consequential while keeping the doorway readable in depth.
cinematographyContract.cameraHeight: Low to the hollow floor, aligned with Bo’s hands and decision objects.
cinematographyContract.composition: Foreground conker and satchel anchor the frame; Bo occupies the warm middle of the hollow; the open door interrupts the curve of the room behind him.
cinematographyContract.depthStrategy: Depth is pressure: manageable objects in front, Bo in the middle, outside day waiting behind.
cinematographyContract.cameraBehavior: Still enough to feel domestic, with tiny hesitant adjustments following Bo’s attention back to the conker instead of toward the door.
cinematographyContract.focusStrategy: Hold the conker and satchel sharp with Bo, allowing the doorway to remain legible but slightly less graspable until Mum’s voice makes it active.
cinematographyContract.lightingFunction: Honeyed interior warmth protects Bo while doorway light quietly asks for forward motion.
cinematographyContract.paletteFunction: Warm browns and golds enclose the room; the exterior light carries a cooler, larger note without becoming hostile.
cinematographyContract.performanceVisibility: Hands, eyeline, and small retractions must be readable; do not bury the delay in broad facial fear.
cinematographyContract.editorialPurpose: Start the sequence from inside the ritual so later interruptions feel like changes to Bo’s private system.
cinematographyContract.memorableLandingImage: Bo in the warm hollow with the decision objects close and the doorway still unanswered.
cinematographyContract.providerInstruction: Start low inside the hollow across the conker and satchel toward Bo, keep the open doorway readable in bright depth, and let Bo’s small paw hesitations carry the delay as Mum’s offscreen call turns the room into a question.

performanceBudget.rationale: The unit carries one clear turn from cosy morning to reversible delay, with enough silence for object glances and the offscreen call to land.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Introduce Bo’s delay and make the hollow oak an active participant in the argument about leaving.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Safe but curious: will he go now?
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Recognition of avoidance disguised as routine.
storyIntent.outerAction: Bo stays by the satchel and conker after Mum calls, promising only a minute.
storyIntent.innerAction: He shrinks the day down to touchable objects so he does not have to face the doorway yet.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play control failing quietly: reach, reconsider, answer politely, then retreat attention to the conker.
storyIntent.mutedRead: Without sound, the audience sees an open door asking for movement and Bo choosing the conker and satchel instead.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The open doorway, lunch satchel, and Mum’s offscreen presence all press him toward leaving while the hollow curves hold him in.
storyIntent.soundStory: Mum’s voice comes from beyond the room; small conker and satchel sounds should feel oversized in the quiet hollow.
storyIntent.motifUse: The conker begins as Bo’s decision switch, a small object carrying too much responsibility.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: Bo changes from resting in the room to using the room to postpone the day; cut when the next thought becomes testing the door for real.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo is not lazy; he is delaying because leaving has emotional weight.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: The specific tail fear remains unrevealed.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Bo’s reaction to Mum’s call changes the room from safe to pressuring.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Mum is close in care but physically offscreen; Bo is alone with his objects.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Mum supplies ordinary morning authority without threat; Bo controls only the timing inside the room.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: Bo touches or hovers near the conker and satchel while avoiding the doorway.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Bo’s eyeline may ricochet between objects and door, but the camera should not make him stare bravely outward yet.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: A small figure held inside a round hollow while a tall bright opening waits beyond.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect small silences after Mum’s call and after Bo’s answer so the audience feels the delay beneath the words.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Keep score minimal or absent; let voice, room tone, and object sounds introduce the motif without telling the audience how to feel.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo sits compactly beside the satchel and conker, paws hovering as if one touch could settle the morning. The offscreen household prompt makes him glance toward the doorway, but his body answers by shrinking back toward the controllable objects; after speaking, he re-centers on the conker like it is safer than the threshold.
shots.animationTiming: Keep the movements small and separated by tiny hesitations: glance, paw hover, retraction, object focus. Let the doorway pressure register in stillness rather than broad alarm.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo tries to keep departure reversible by making the room’s smallest objects feel more reachable than the open threshold.

phases.observableAction: Warm hollow surfaces hold Bo close while the bright open doorway remains visible behind him as a vertical interruption.
Bo’s paws hover near the satchel, pull back, and return toward the conker as his eyeline flicks from object to doorway and back.
After the offscreen prompt, Bo keeps his body low and tidy instead of rising toward the threshold.
Bo remains beside the satchel and conker, angled inward, with the open doorway still unanswered behind him.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The offscreen household call makes the doorway active; Bo’s eyeline checks it, but his hands choose the satchel and conker, so his body stays inside and the threshold remains uncrossed.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo shifts from resting in a safe room to using the room’s objects to delay movement.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo must end visibly inside the hollow, close to the conker and satchel, with the doorway still waiting in depth.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Allow variation in blink cadence, paw tremble, tail settling, and the exact size of each hesitation, as long as Bo never appears ready to stride out.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo is a warm, nimble young squirrel whose worry shows through quick paws, small pauses, and an expressive tail.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants to keep the morning small enough to handle by staying near his satchel and conker.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: Under the offscreen prompt, he gets tidier and smaller, touching or almost touching objects instead of crossing space.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Paws close to chest, quick eyeline ricochet, compact posture, tail contained within the room’s curve.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would lean toward the opening and gather nerve through forward motion; Bo’s squirrel-specific delay is a retreat into small reachable objects.

stagePlan.purpose: Make the doorway too large for Bo’s current courage.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo places the conker in the bag and reaches the open door, but the threshold freezes him and sends him back toward tomorrow.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The first real attempt to leave collapses into retreat.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to the threshold already looming in the frame, then let the camera stop with Bo when his body stops.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo is frozen at the open door, unable to step through.

stagePlan.purpose: Convert retreat into the conker decision-game.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo scurries back inside, takes the conker out, then talks himself toward today and puts it back into the bag.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: A tiny hopeful verdict appears: today could be manageable.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Follow the conker’s path back from the bag to Bo’s paws and back again, keeping the doorway in relation so the audience tracks the loop.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The conker is back in the bag and Bo has briefly recommitted to today.

stagePlan.purpose: Let the game turn into a panic machine.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo’s anxiety rises again, he pulls the conker out once more, and the final question bursts through the ritual.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The joke of the switch flips into vulnerability; deciding harder makes him less in control.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Tighten around Bo, conker, satchel, and doorway without losing geography, ending on the conker held too tightly.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo clutches the conker with visible panic, the satchel and doorway still unresolved.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Give the door its first physical victory over Bo.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: Threshold-facing view from inside the hollow, close enough that Bo’s stop feels bodily rather than scenic.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: Bo puts the conker in the bag, approaches the open door, opens it, freezes, and begins bargaining for tomorrow.
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: The body reaches commitment and then locks: breath caught, paws pulled close, momentum gone.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: Bo stopped at the open doorway with the bag near him and no step taken outside.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: Changed emotional state and scale of pressure: the doorway is no longer background, it is the obstacle.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Make the conker physically operate as the decision switch.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: Object-led view at satchel height, travelling only enough to follow conker in, conker out, conker in while the doorway remains spatially readable.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: Bo retreats, removes the conker, admits today could be possible, sighs, and puts the conker back.
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: Fussy overcommitment: careful hands try to make the tiny object produce certainty.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: The conker sits inside the satchel as Bo briefly steadies himself.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: New visual idea: the argument transfers from doorway to object loop.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Let the loop fail and expose the panic underneath.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: Closer on Bo with the conker held between him and the open-room depth; the frame has less breathing room than before.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: The thought that today might not be okay returns; Bo pulls the conker out again and asks, “What if it’s not OK?!”
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: Control frays: the paws stop being tidy, the conker is gripped instead of placed, and the line breaks the rhythm.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: Bo clutching the conker while the bag and open doorway remain unfinished business.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: The final panic beat earns a fresh boundary because the next event is an outside presence interrupting the private loop.

shots.purpose: Escalate the conker from comfort object to comic decision machine, then let the machine trap Bo.
shots.audienceExperience: Children play the in-out suspense of the conker; adults feel the exhausting loop of rehearsed courage turning against itself.
shots.openingImage: Bo’s paw sets the conker into the satchel while the open doorway waits just ahead.
shots.principalPerformance: Bo must never become broadly frantic too early; the comedy comes from treating each conker placement with grave seriousness until the ritual cannot contain him.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera behaves like worry: it approaches the door, recoils into the object loop, then tightens as the loop stops helping.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: Bo moves from possible departure to repeated reversal, ending more trapped than at the start.
shots.closingImage: Bo holds the conker close against himself, with the satchel open and the doorway still visible beyond.
shots.transitionReason: A cut is stronger than staying continuous because Keen’s knock changes the scene from private ritual to witnessed exposure. If the camera simply waited through the doorway, the shock of another presence entering Bo’s sealed loop would soften.
shots.providerBoundaryExplanation: This unit’s natural 25 seconds plus the next unit’s natural 13 seconds would exceed 30 seconds; Keen’s arrival also needs a fresh first frame organized around the doorway interruption rather than the conker loop.

cinematographyContract.storyPointOfView: Bo’s worry as it tries to turn a giant social fear into a small repeatable object action.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceStart: Close but still able to see the path to the door.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceEnd: Tighter and more cornered, sharing Bo’s inability to find a stable verdict.
cinematographyContract.revealStrategy: Reveal panic through failed repetitions before naming the deeper fear.
cinematographyContract.shotScale: Starts as a body-and-threshold medium, compresses into object-and-hands intimacy.
cinematographyContract.lensIntent: Keep the conker tactile and important without making it magical; maintain enough depth for the door to remain the true pressure.
cinematographyContract.cameraHeight: Low at Bo’s hand and satchel height, rising only slightly when the doorway freezes him.
cinematographyContract.composition: The frame loops between three anchors: conker, satchel, doorway; each return feels less cosy and more trapped.
cinematographyContract.depthStrategy: Use depth as a treadmill: every conker move relates back to the same unresolved doorway behind or ahead.
cinematographyContract.cameraBehavior: Pursues Bo to the threshold, retreats with him, then lingers on the repeated object path until the pattern breaks.
cinematographyContract.focusStrategy: Focus follows the decision object when it changes state, then returns to Bo’s grip when the object no longer settles him.
cinematographyContract.lightingFunction: Doorway light remains constant; the emotional change comes from Bo’s changing distance to it.
cinematographyContract.paletteFunction: Warm interior holds, but tighter framing lets the brighter doorway feel more intrusive.
cinematographyContract.performanceVisibility: Hands, shoulders, breath, and the precise conker state must be readable at every reversal.
cinematographyContract.editorialPurpose: Build the comic meter of decision and reversal until the audience feels the ritual fail.
cinematographyContract.memorableLandingImage: The conker clutched like a giant answer it cannot provide.
cinematographyContract.providerInstruction: Track the conker’s in-out-in-out journey between Bo’s paws and the satchel while keeping the open doorway spatially present; let the frame tighten only as Bo’s tidy decision ritual breaks into panic.

performanceBudget.rationale: Three dialogue turns, four conker state changes, a threshold freeze, and a panic landing need the full unit but remain one causal loop under 30 seconds.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Show Bo’s delay escalating into a self-tightening panic ritual.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Suspenseful fun: which way will the conker decide?
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Empathy for a child trapped by the need to make the perfect decision.
storyIntent.outerAction: Bo approaches the door, freezes, retreats, and repeatedly moves the conker in and out of the satchel.
storyIntent.innerAction: He tries to outsource courage to a tiny object because accepting uncertainty feels too big.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play each reversal as sincere logic in Bo’s head, not random fussing; the panic arrives because the logic keeps failing.
storyIntent.mutedRead: The conker’s repeated state changes and Bo’s freeze at the doorway clearly show a decision loop becoming distress.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The doorway keeps its position as the unfinished step; the satchel waits as proof he should already be leaving.
storyIntent.soundStory: Conker taps, satchel rustles, a held breath at the threshold, then the final line breaking the rhythm.
storyIntent.motifUse: The conker is now fully the decision switch: in means today, out means retreat, neither works.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: Bo changes from believing one more conker choice can settle him to realising no choice has made today safe; cut when an outside witness is about to break the private system.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo’s panic is real even though the conker loop is funny.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: The audience still does not fully know that the tail is the specific social fear.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Bo’s reaction to the threshold changes the meaning of the door from exit to test.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Bo is alone; the absent world presses through the open door rather than through another body.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: The conker briefly holds pretend authority because Bo grants it authority.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: Bo touches the conker repeatedly and avoids stepping through the doorway.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: His eyeline should keep betraying the true problem by returning to the door after each object choice.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: A small body circling between a low object and a tall opening, then tightening around the object.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the freeze at the threshold and the tiny pause before the final panic question.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: If score is present, let it pulse lightly with the conker loop and thin out before the final panic, never covering the object sounds.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo places the conker with careful seriousness and makes his first real approach to the open door, but his momentum stops at the threshold. He scurries back into the room and turns the conker into a repeated in-and-out ritual: each placement is precise at first, then faster, less tidy, and finally a tight clutch against his chest.
shots.animationTiming: Start with measured, sincere object handling; hold the threshold freeze long enough for breath to catch. The conker loop should accelerate by commitment, not speed alone, ending with a squeezed hold and a broken rhythm.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo tries to force certainty out of one repeatable object action, but every result sends him back into another reversal.

phases.observableAction: Bo sets the conker into the satchel, gathers himself, and moves toward the open doorway with careful, contained steps.
At the threshold Bo locks in place, then retreats and repeatedly transfers the conker between his paws and the satchel.
Each reversal leaves his shoulders higher, paws less neat, and grip tighter around the conker.
Bo ends clutching the conker close, with the satchel open and the doorway still visible beyond him.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The threshold stops Bo’s forward motion; retreat puts him back at the satchel, where each conker placement or removal creates the next opposite action until the object is gripped rather than placed.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: A tidy departure attempt becomes a self-tightening object loop, then breaks into visible distress.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo must finish with the conker held too tightly against himself, the satchel unresolved, and the doorway still spatially clear.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: The exact path of the scurry, number of tiny paw adjustments, tail counterbalance, and breath pattern may vary, but the conker state changes must remain unmistakable.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s worry and curiosity pull him into quick, sincere, object-focused behaviour; his tail and paws reveal what he cannot settle.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants the conker to make the outside step feel decided and safe.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: When the doorway confronts him, he freezes, retreats, and overcommits to the repeated object action.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Light squirrel steps, abrupt stop, paws gathering the conker carefully at first and clutching it by the end, tail balancing each reversal.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen under pressure would show a gulp and step through; Bo uniquely turns pressure into a fussy decision ritual around his satchel and conker.

comedyStaging.staysVisible: The conker, Bo’s paws, the lunch satchel and the open doorway remain readable in relation to one another so the audience tracks the decision loop and the pressure of the exit.
comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: Each conker move has small tactile weight: paw pads gather it, set it down or pull it back; the satchel shifts only when Bo actually touches or bumps it, proving the room is responding to his fussy momentum.
comedyStaging.payoffShape: A repeated in-out pattern tightens into faster, less tidy reversals until Bo’s body freezes and the final line pops out as the ritual fails him.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the conker into a magical chooser or animated character.
Do not make the loop so fast that the audience loses where the doorway is.
Do not cut away from the conker’s final position before Bo’s panic lands.

stagePlan.purpose: Introduce Keen as a gentle interruption rather than an invasion.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: A shadow reaches the doorway, Keen gently taps on the hollow tree and peeks inside, changing the private room into a shared threshold.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The outside world arrives softly, but it still arrives.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to the doorway from Bo’s interior perspective, discovering Keen only when the room does.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Keen is present at the doorway, paused and not pushing in.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn Bo’s private control into visible startle without making Keen unsafe.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo jumps, the conker flies, he catches and fumbles it into a hug, then looks from the conker to Keen as Keen explains Aida sent him.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The startle is funny, but the softness of Keen’s delivery keeps it from becoming humiliation.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Let the conker’s flight briefly lead the eye, then settle into a shared threshold composition.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo hugs the conker inside the room while Keen remains gently at the doorway.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Make Keen’s entrance a discovered presence inside Bo’s point of view.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: Interior view toward the doorway; the knock enters before the frame fully admits Keen, preserving Bo’s startle.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: A shadow appears, Keen taps a gentle shave-and-a-haircut knock, peeks in, holds a beat, and says, “Hi! I'm Keen.”
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: Keen’s body stays soft and available; the knock behaves like it knows the room can be startled.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: Keen at the doorway with space between him and Bo’s interior.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: New information and altered privacy: another character now occupies the threshold.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Pay off the startle and show the conker losing authority.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: Quick object-follow within the same unit as the conker pops up and Bo fumbles it, then settle to include Bo’s hug and Keen’s doorway position.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: Bo jumps, the conker flies, he catches it after several fumbles, hugs it, and immediately looks from it to Keen while Keen says, “Aida sent me. She thought we should meet.”
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: Bo’s panic is in the overlarge recovery; Keen’s calm is in not advancing after the startle.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: Bo clutching the conker, Keen still outside the room’s center at the threshold.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: The view changes from entrance discovery to consequence of interruption; it is comic punctuation and altered power.

shots.purpose: Break Bo’s private loop with a kind witness at the exact place he fears.
shots.audienceExperience: A startle-laugh followed by relief: the interruption exposes Bo, but Keen does not barge in or judge him.
shots.openingImage: The open doorway from inside the hollow as a soft shadow touches its edge.
shots.principalPerformance: Keen enters with gentle curiosity; Bo’s body reacts before his social self can tidy it up.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera discovers Keen with Bo, then steadies enough to prove Keen is not a threat.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: The conker stops being a private decision tool and becomes something Bo clutches while another person is present.
shots.closingImage: Bo hugging the conker inside the hollow while Keen waits at the threshold.
shots.transitionReason: A cut is stronger than remaining continuous because the next unit is not about the entrance but the real fear being spoken and made visible by the tail. A fresh setup lets the audience feel the room inhale before exposure.
shots.providerBoundaryExplanation: This unit’s natural 13 seconds plus the next unit’s natural 23 seconds would exceed 30 seconds, and the next unit needs its own performance space for the fear, tail action, silence, and awe to breathe.

cinematographyContract.storyPointOfView: Bo’s startled discovery of a gentle witness.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceStart: Inside Bo’s sealed room, wary of the threshold.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceEnd: Still with Bo, but now able to hold Keen as a calm presence rather than only doorway pressure.
cinematographyContract.revealStrategy: Reveal Keen as a soft shadow and knock before a full social encounter, so the startle belongs to Bo’s state, not to Keen being aggressive.
cinematographyContract.shotScale: Threshold medium with a brief object-comedy insert created by the conker’s flight inside the same unit.
cinematographyContract.lensIntent: Let the doorway feel newly occupied without making Keen loom over Bo.
cinematographyContract.cameraHeight: Interior child-height, near Bo’s scale, looking toward the doorway.
cinematographyContract.composition: Bo’s interior warmth and Keen’s threshold position share the frame only after the conker startle proves the room has been interrupted.
cinematographyContract.depthStrategy: Keen occupies the background threshold first; the conker’s flight briefly crosses the depth between private object and outside witness.
cinematographyContract.cameraBehavior: Hesitates at the doorway, flinches with the conker, then settles into a witness position.
cinematographyContract.focusStrategy: Focus discovers Keen on the knock, snaps with the conker’s flight, then returns to Bo’s hug and Keen’s calm relation.
cinematographyContract.lightingFunction: The doorway light outlines the arrival but does not turn brighter; Keen changes its meaning by how softly he stands in it.
cinematographyContract.paletteFunction: Maintain warm interior against exterior light, beginning the shift from boundary to meeting place.
cinematographyContract.performanceVisibility: Bo’s fumble sequence and Keen’s non-invasive stillness must both read in the same emotional breath.
cinematographyContract.editorialPurpose: Turn the private decision game into social exposure while keeping Keen safe.
cinematographyContract.memorableLandingImage: Bo clutching the conker while Keen waits kindly at the doorway.
cinematographyContract.providerInstruction: From inside the hollow, discover Keen as a soft doorway shadow and gentle knock; let Bo’s startled conker fumble play clearly, then land with Bo hugging the conker while Keen remains calmly at the threshold.

performanceBudget.rationale: The entrance, beat, startle, conker fumble, and Keen’s explanation form one interruption arc and can breathe under 30 seconds.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Introduce Keen as the first witness to Bo’s delay without making him a rescuer.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Relief that the new presence is gentle.
storyIntent.outerAction: Keen knocks and introduces himself; Bo jumps, fumbles the conker, and hugs it.
storyIntent.innerAction: Bo’s private control is exposed before he can choose a composed version of himself.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Keen should make himself smaller than the doorway; Bo should overprotect the conker after losing it in the air.
storyIntent.mutedRead: A gentle arrival startles Bo so hard his decision object flies, but the newcomer stays at the boundary instead of invading.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The doorway becomes embodied by Keen, turning abstract outside pressure into a relationship possibility.
storyIntent.soundStory: The knock should be playful but soft; the conker fumble supplies the comic texture; Keen’s voice lowers the room’s alarm.
storyIntent.motifUse: The conker’s flight shows the decision switch has lost control the moment a real witness appears.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: Bo changes from managing a private object loop to being seen; cut when that exposure must become the spoken social fear.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Keen is connected to Aida and has come kindly, not to inspect or fix Bo.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: Keen has not yet seen the tail do the feared thing.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Bo’s oversized startle changes Keen’s entrance from simple greeting to exposure of Bo’s panic.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Keen remains at the threshold; Bo remains deeper inside, with distance protecting both of them.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Keen has social confidence but gives Bo space; Bo holds the room’s vulnerability.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: Bo hugs the conker; Keen avoids crossing the threshold uninvited.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Bo’s eyes must jump from conker to Keen so the audience understands both the object and the new witness matter.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: One figure tucked inside with a small object, one figure softened by the doorway.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the beat after the knock before Keen speaks, and the tiny settle after the fumble.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Withhold score or keep it nearly absent; let the knock and fumble provide rhythm, then soften under Keen’s second line.

shots.physicalPerformance: Keen appears as a soft presence at the doorway: he taps lightly, peeks in, and keeps his weight outside the room’s center. Bo jolts before he can compose himself; the conker pops free, bounces through several fumbled catches, and ends hugged tight as Bo checks the object and then Keen.
shots.animationTiming: Let the knock breathe before Keen fully reads. Bo’s startle should be quick and springy, followed by a comic fumble with clear catches and slips, then a gentle settle that proves Keen is not advancing.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Keen offers entry as gently as possible; Bo’s body reveals how sealed and overwound the private loop has become.

phases.observableAction: Keen holds at the threshold, taps softly on the hollow, and peeks in without crossing into the room.
Bo jumps, launching the conker upward, then fumbles it through several catches before trapping it against his body.
Bo’s eyes snap from the hugged conker to Keen, measuring the object loss and the new witness in one quick check.
Keen remains calmly at the doorway with soft posture and no forward step after Bo’s startle.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s soft doorway knock interrupts the private loop; Bo’s startle sends the conker into the air, forcing a messy recovery, and Keen’s stillness prevents the interruption from becoming a chase into the room.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo’s private control becomes witnessed exposure, but Keen’s body language keeps the encounter gentle.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo must end hugging the conker inside the hollow while Keen waits at the threshold, leaving space between them.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Allow play in the conker’s arc, Bo’s fumble pattern, and Keen’s micro-softening, provided the startle is Bo’s oversize response and Keen does not crowd him.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Keen is forward and curious, but real courage for him includes softness before action rather than fearless pushing.
characterTruths.playableWant: Keen wants to make contact without startling the room more than necessary.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo's Mum
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Offscreen Mum: warm household steadiness, practical but listening for Bo’s hesitation; not scolding, not sugary.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Nudge Bo toward the doorway while keeping the morning ordinary enough that he can step into it.
voicePerformances.subtext: I know this is big, so I’m making it sound like a normal leaving-the-house moment.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo, from another room, close enough to care but giving him space.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Busy morning warmth with a faint check-in underneath.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Hopeful that the gentle prompt will move him, but leaving room for his reply.
voicePerformances.pace: Unhurried domestic call; soften slightly on the question mark after Learning Circle.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Two-part call: first the real nudge, then the everyday lunch reminder as emotional cover.
voicePerformances.pauses: Tiny settling pause after “BO,” so it is a loving call-in, not a bark; brief lift before “Don’t forget” to make the lunch tag feel practical.
voicePerformances.breaths: Small breath before the second sentence, like she is moving through the house while speaking.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Heard offscreen; her voice creates the doorway pressure that makes Bo glance over, then shrink back to the conker.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: [quietly] BO, it’s TIME for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your LUNCH.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Her calm voice contrasts Bo’s tiny, controlled body; the ordinariness of her delivery makes his stillness read louder.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Begin after Bo’s paws hover over the objects; let the line arrive from offscreen, then leave a beat for his glance toward the doorway.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: I’ll go in a minute Mum.
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo: small, careful, self-managing; tries to sound reasonable while his breath betrays the pressure.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Buy time from Mum without letting her hear how stuck he is.
voicePerformances.subtext: If I say it tidily, maybe I can stay in this safe little circle a bit longer.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo’s Mum offscreen, with the conker as his safer secondary listener.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Startled by the prompt, shrinking back toward control.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Momentarily relieved, but more attached to the conker than before.
voicePerformances.pace: Soft and contained; slightly too quick on “I’ll go,” then slow on “in a minute.”
voicePerformances.rhythm: A neat little sentence trying to behave; the final “Mum” asks not to be pushed.
voicePerformances.pauses: No big pause inside the line; the hesitation belongs before it as his glance retracts from the doorway.
voicePerformances.breaths: Tiny inhale before “I’ll,” held shallow through the line.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Paws hover, retract, then return toward the conker as he answers.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: [nervous] I’ll go in a MINUTE Mum.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice performs compliance while the body chooses the objects; the mismatch reveals the fear without naming it.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Do not start on the offscreen cue. Let Bo glance toward the doorway, hover a paw, then answer as he pulls back.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: Maybe, I’ll go tomorrow instead. Tomorrow sounds much better than today. Tomorrow everything will OK, not today.
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo: anxious logic-maker; treating each thought like a careful conker placement that might make the day safe.

voicePerformances.subtext: Tomorrow is imaginary, so tomorrow can’t hurt me.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Mostly himself and the conker; Mum is distant in his mind, the doorway is the threat.

voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Less tidy; the repetition comforts him but also winds him tighter.
