voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Room softened by the joke, Bo almost ready but not fully confident.
voicePerformances.pace: Calm and inviting; second sentence reassuring but not preachy.
voicePerformances.rhythm: First sentence opens the door; second sentence cushions the step.
voicePerformances.pauses: Small pause between sentences; leave a little space after “walk” if Bo is watching the doorway.
voicePerformances.breaths: Easy breath before “Fresh air,” as if the idea itself makes the room bigger.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen keeps the offer soft, allowing Bo to look, loosen, set the conker down, and let the tail deflate in stages.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: Let’s go for a WALK and get some FRESH AIR. Fresh air always HELPS.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice creates a modest path out, matching Bo’s staged release rather than rushing him into bravery.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Begin after Bo has reacted to the still-tail gag; allow the line to cover the first stage of Bo’s loosening, not the final exit.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo: cautious relief; not fixed, just willing to take the next small step.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Accept Keen’s offer without pretending the fear has disappeared.
voicePerformances.subtext: I can try this if it stays this gentle.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen, with one last private goodbye to the conker as safety object.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Softened by being witnessed and by Keen’s harmless silliness.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Small readiness; fear still carried, but moving.
voicePerformances.pace: Slow, shy, with a tiny warmth blooming on “nice.”
voicePerformances.rhythm: One careful agreement; the smile arrives late.
voicePerformances.pauses: Pre-line pause as Bo looks from Keen’s tail to his own, then to the conker; no internal pause.
voicePerformances.breaths: Quiet release-breath before “That,” like the grip has finally let go.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Bo studies, loosens, sets the conker down without ceremony, tail softens, then he moves out with Keen as the satchel lifts.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The exhale is the physical release of the conker and the tail’s softening; voice remains modest so the fear is not magically erased.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: After the staged release has begun: look, loosen, set down; let “nice” coincide with the almost-smile before the modest move toward the doorway.

direction.premise: Bo wants to make it to the Learning Circle without anyone noticing the big nervous thing his tail does; instead, being witnessed kindly turns the tail from a problem to a doorway into friendship.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo step toward a group who already know each other while letting the part of himself he wants to hide be seen?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is met with delight instead of judgement.
direction.externalJourney: Keen is pulled from a failed honey sneak to help Bo leave his hollow tree, walk through the Whispering Woods, arrive at the Learning Circle, share his tail trick with the group, and end the day with a new friend.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from postponing and repacking to taking one small step, then another, until his tail is no longer an alarm bell but a playful part of him he can offer to others.
direction.relationshipChanges: Keen shifts from mischievous solo adventurer to gentle witness and walking companion; Aida becomes the steady elder who normalises going while wobbly; the Learning Circle moves from imagined judgement to real delight; Fuzzby remains the comic mirror of failed sneaking, now turned back on himself.
direction.emotionalCurve: Playful sneakiness opens the episode, then Aida’s quiet vision redirects the story into Bo’s small domestic worry. The middle rises through stop-start panic, is softened by Keen’s admiration and Aida’s honesty, then glows into movement. The Learning Circle brings the feared exposure, but it lands as welcome. The final garden gag releases the episode with the honeycomb still untouched and friendship quietly proved.
direction.comedyCurve: Physical suspense in the honeycomb sneaking gives way to sneeze comedy, then to Bo’s conker-packing loop and tail poof escalation. Keen’s dead-still tail reverses the embarrassment into shared silliness. Sunny’s over-bright welcome and Luna’s tiny brake reset the group rhythm, and Fuzzby’s flower disguise pays off the opening honeycomb challenge with a self-inflicted crash.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s warning in Scene 1 return as the final garden button in Scene 8. Bo’s conker-packing loop sets up his stop-start threshold fear, which pays off in his first steps on the glowing path. The tail’s first unwanted poof becomes a chosen game in the woods, then a group celebration at the Learning Circle, then the shared drawing joke. Aida’s vision of Bo not moving pays off in Aida and Keen helping him move without forcing him.
direction.visualMotifs: Thresholds, satchel-in/satchel-out, the conker in Bo’s paws, Bo’s tail expanding and softening, leaves and forest paths, pink-and-blue light joining on the ground, and the honeycomb sitting untouched as a comic measuring stick of growth.
direction.sonicMotifs: Tiny crunches and pops begin as sneaky danger; Bo’s tail poofs become softer and more playful; Aida’s rose-quartz bowl tone opens the unseen need; Keen’s aquamarine note joins Aida’s warmth on the path; Zenny’s low meditation hum bookends the bee comedy.
direction.climax: On the forest path, Aida’s rose light and Keen’s blue light join, and Bo takes step after step with them, repeating Aida’s phrase back as an action rather than a lesson.
direction.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail does the thing in front of everyone and the group responds with curiosity and delight; later, Bo and Keen draw and laugh together while Aida watches from the edge, pendant glowing softly.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, lightly funny relief: the room should feel that Bo did not become a different squirrel; he became seen, and the honeycomb button lets the audience leave laughing without erasing the cost of the day.

storyTruth.falseBelief: If the group sees the part of him that poofs and panics, they will not want him there.
storyTruth.practicalWant: Delay leaving home, then get to the Learning Circle without his tail drawing attention.
storyTruth.keyRelationship: Bo and Keen, with Aida as the elder witness who turns going while worried into something ordinary and brave.
storyTruth.emotionalFearOrWound: Bo fears being the unknown one among friends who already belong to each other.
storyTruth.transformedAction: Bo walks through the door, steps down the glowing path, and lets his tail poof in front of the group as something they can enjoy with him.
storyTruth.themeProvenThroughAction: The thing Bo hides becomes the thing he shares, and sharing it is what lets the group welcome him.

transformationMap.believes: Getting the honeycomb or getting out the door should be possible if he is quiet enough, careful enough, or delayed enough.
transformationMap.feels: Playful on the surface, but easily startled when the world notices him.
transformationMap.does: Keen sneaks; Bo repacks and postpones, using the conker and satchel as reasons not to cross the threshold.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Keen is alone in mischief; Bo is alone with his worry; Aida has only sensed the need from a distance.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Giggles first, then recognition of the small trapped feeling of not being ready.

transformationMap.believes: Today might go wrong, and the safest move is to try again tomorrow.
transformationMap.feels: Cornered by the doorway and by the thought of being seen.
transformationMap.does: Bo opens the door, freezes, retreats, removes the conker, replaces it, and spirals around the satchel until Keen appears.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Bo’s Mum can only nudge from offscreen; Keen arrives as an unexpected witness rather than a fixer.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Tender amusement at the loop, with a small gasp when Bo gets stuck at the door.

transformationMap.believes: If the tail does the thing, it proves something is wrong with him.
transformationMap.feels: Embarrassed, exposed, and braced for judgement.
transformationMap.does: Bo grabs at his tail and begs it to behave; Keen looks impressed instead of alarmed, then makes his own still tail into the joke.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Keen becomes safe because he admires what Bo fears and makes himself look silly first.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Relief through laughter: the strange thing becomes wonderful for a moment.

transformationMap.believes: Maybe the tail can be played with, but the Learning Circle is still the real unknown.
transformationMap.feels: Buoyant while the game works, then small again when the path ahead returns.
transformationMap.does: Bo poofs the tail on command, giggles, then stops and sits when the bigger social fear comes back.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Keen can accompany him, but cannot make the group less unknown; Bo needs an older truth from Aida.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: The lift drops into a quiet ache, because the joke did not magically remove the worry.

transformationMap.believes: Everyone there already belongs, and he does not.
transformationMap.feels: Still, tight, satchel-gripping, looking down the path from the outside.
transformationMap.does: Bo says the true problem aloud while Keen sits beside him and Aida sits with space, not pressure.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Aida joins as a grounded witness; the group is still offscreen and imagined, which makes it feel larger.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: A held breath: this is the one quiet centre where the child sees Bo stuck and the adult feels the old doorway fear.

transformationMap.believes: Going can happen even while the wobbly feeling comes too.
transformationMap.feels: Not fixed, but accompanied.
transformationMap.does: Bo accepts the offered paw-light, watches Aida and Keen let their crystals answer, and takes one step, then another, down the glowing path.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Bo is not carried or corrected; he is walked with, between rose confidence and blue courage.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Hopeful release: the path itself seems to say the next step is enough.

transformationMap.believes: The tail thing can be part of how others know and enjoy him.
transformationMap.feels: Open, delighted, still carrying a trace of the morning’s cost.
transformationMap.does: Bo lets the tail poof at the Learning Circle, draws the joke into Keen’s picture, and laughs with a friend while Aida watches from the edge.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Bo has moved from visitor to participant; Keen has become his friend; Aida’s role softens from guide to proud witness.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Belonging with a laugh still attached, not a clean reset.

tapestryMap.physicalMotifArc: Hands hover over honey, satchel, conker and tail at first; by the middle, paws sit beside rather than grab; by the end, the tail moves freely and playfully in open space.
tapestryMap.visualMotifArc: Closed circles and thresholds dominate early: honeycomb, snore bubbles, hollow door, satchel mouth, conker. These open into the winding path, then into the Learning Circle, and finally a wide golden garden where the honeycomb remains untouched.
tapestryMap.colourAndLightJourney: Warm golden morning starts mischievous and safe; Aida’s scene adds rose mist and inner light; Bo’s hollow is warm but enclosed; the woods use dappled green-gold with worry sitting in shadow; the crystal path blends rose and azure; the Learning Circle is sunny and communal; the final garden settles into golden sunset.
tapestryMap.sourceSoundArc: Crunches, pops, sneezes and offscreen calls make the world startle the characters early. Mid-episode, footsteps and rustling leaves slow the pace. The climax lets crystal tones and path ambience take over. The ending returns to buzz-crash and meditation hum as comic release.
tapestryMap.musicMotifArc: Begin with plucky sneak pizzicato and tiny bee buzz rhythm, move into Aida’s low rose-quartz bowl tone, then a small squirrel motif around the conker. Keen’s B note and Aida’s G note join on the path, with a light circle-theme emerging once Bo is welcomed. The final cue pares down to a warm sunset button with bee comic accents.
tapestryMap.environmentalMetaphor: Homes, honeycombs and bags are safe containers; the path is the uncertain middle; the circle is the feared social world that proves soft; the garden ending shows the world unchanged, but Bo and Keen’s relationship has changed inside it.
tapestryMap.openingImage: Keen in golden dew tiptoeing toward an untouched honeycomb while Fuzzby sleeps directly on top of the prize.
tapestryMap.finalImage: A wide golden garden: the honeycomb still untouched, Fuzzby tangled in flower petals nearby, and the day’s warmth resting over a joke that no longer feels lonely.
tapestryMap.transformedMeaning: The same world that first popped, startled and blocked the characters becomes a place where surprises can be shared, witnessed and laughed with.

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Keen tries to get honey; Aida senses Bo and redirects Keen toward helping him.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: Keen’s body betrays the sneak with pollen and sneezes; Aida’s vision reveals a child who cannot move forward.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Aida connects the comic sneeze outside her clearing to the real need inside Bo’s hollow.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Keen is summoned to go with Aida’s purpose behind him.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: Who is the squirrel in the vision, and why can’t he leave?

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Bo must leave home for the Learning Circle.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalStart: Warm domestic safety with a small trapped delay.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: The satchel, conker and open door become a loop that keeps Bo from leaving; Keen’s arrival exposes him.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Keen’s impressed response to the tail thing changes Bo’s feared exposure into a first moment of being liked.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Bo smiles and walks out with Keen.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: Can that tiny confidence survive the walk to the group?

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Keen, Bo and Aida need to keep moving toward the Learning Circle.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalStart: Playful recovery as Bo performs the tail poof on purpose.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: The sight of the path brings back the fear of entering a group who already knows each other.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Aida sits beside Bo, admits through action and simple presence that going can still happen every time, and joins her rose light with Keen’s blue light.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Bo takes steps down the glowing path with them.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: Will the group actually welcome the thing Bo feared?

sequenceBlueprint.externalObjective: Bo meets the bears and finds his place in the Learning Circle.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalStart: Big welcoming energy that could overwhelm him.
sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: Sunny’s brightness, everyone watching, and Bo’s tail poof create the exact exposure he feared.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Misty and Amie respond with curiosity and delight, turning the tail into a shared game; later Bo and Keen draw and laugh as friends.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Aida watches Bo belong without needing to manage the moment.
sequenceBlueprint.dominantAudienceFeeling: Joyful acceptance, with the parent seeing how little it took: one kind reaction.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: How does the episode release the honeycomb setup and leave us laughing?

sequenceBlueprint.pressureOrComplication: Fuzzby’s flower disguise cannot overcome his own full-throttle clumsiness.
sequenceBlueprint.emotionalTurn: Keen effortlessly repeats Fuzzby’s opening warning back at him, and Zenny’s tiny smile lets affection leak through the deadpan.
sequenceBlueprint.endCondition: Fuzzby is stuck in petals, Zenny returns to stillness, and the honeycomb remains untouched.
sequenceBlueprint.dominantAudienceFeeling: Clean laugh with a warm afterglow.
sequenceBlueprint.nextQuestion: None; the day rests on a joke that carries the relationship forward.

northStar.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is met with delight instead of judgement.
northStar.childClearWant: Bo wants to not go today because he is scared nobody will like him if his tail acts funny.

scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.purpose: Bo’s private delaying ritual turns from cosy control into exposed panic, then Keen’s gentle witnessing makes one small step toward the doorway possible.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo leave the hollow oak while the tail he wants hidden remains visible and uncontrolled?
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.entry: If I wait a little longer and keep checking, I can avoid today and keep my tail from ruining things.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.exit: Bo leaves the hollow oak with Keen for fresh air, carrying the fear forward instead of resolving it inside the room.

pointOfView: Bo’s private delay ritual, with the world outside present only as voice and doorway pressure.
Bo’s worry as it tries to turn a giant social fear into a small repeatable object action.
Bo’s startled discovery of a gentle witness.
Bo’s feared visibility, transformed by Keen’s wonder.
Bo’s relief as Keen makes being seen survivable, with the conker’s abandonment proving the change.

dramaticBeats.beginning: The room shifts from simple morning safety into a delaying chamber: Mum’s offscreen prompt makes the open doorway active, and Bo answers by keeping the decision reversible through the conker and satchel.
dramaticBeats.development: The conker is no longer in control, and Bo can no longer pretend the delay ritual is private.
dramaticBeats.turn: Keen shows his tail’s uselessness without demanding Bo change, then suggests fresh air; Bo lets the smile grow and agrees.
dramaticBeats.landing: The relief-laugh hands to forward warmth: Bo is not cured, but he is no longer alone at the threshold.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Bo keeps the body tidy and small; every attempt to answer the day sends his paws back to the objects he can control.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Bo sits compactly beside the satchel and conker, paws hovering as if one touch could settle the morning. The offscreen household prompt makes him glance toward the doorway, but his body answers by shrinking back toward the controllable objects; after speaking, he re-centers on the conker like it is safer than the threshold.

contract.playableIntention: Bo tries to keep departure reversible by making the room’s smallest objects feel more reachable than the open threshold.

phases.observableAction: Warm hollow surfaces hold Bo close while the bright open doorway remains visible behind him as a vertical interruption.
Bo’s paws hover near the satchel, pull back, and return toward the conker as his eyeline flicks from object to doorway and back.
After the offscreen prompt, Bo keeps his body low and tidy instead of rising toward the threshold.
Bo remains beside the satchel and conker, angled inward, with the open doorway still unanswered behind him.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The offscreen household call makes the doorway active; Bo’s eyeline checks it, but his hands choose the satchel and conker, so his body stays inside and the threshold remains uncrossed.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo shifts from resting in a safe room to using the room’s objects to delay movement.
contract.requiredLanding: Bo must end visibly inside the hollow, close to the conker and satchel, with the doorway still waiting in depth.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow variation in blink cadence, paw tremble, tail settling, and the exact size of each hesitation, as long as Bo never appears ready to stride out.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo is a warm, nimble young squirrel whose worry shows through quick paws, small pauses, and an expressive tail.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants to keep the morning small enough to handle by staying near his satchel and conker.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: Under the offscreen prompt, he gets tidier and smaller, touching or almost touching objects instead of crossing space.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Paws close to chest, quick eyeline ricochet, compact posture, tail contained within the room’s curve.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would lean toward the opening and gather nerve through forward motion; Bo’s squirrel-specific delay is a retreat into small reachable objects.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Bo must never become broadly frantic too early; the comedy comes from treating each conker placement with grave seriousness until the ritual cannot contain him.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Bo places the conker with careful seriousness and makes his first real approach to the open door, but his momentum stops at the threshold. He scurries back into the room and turns the conker into a repeated in-and-out ritual: each placement is precise at first, then faster, less tidy, and finally a tight clutch against his chest.

contract.playableIntention: Bo tries to force certainty out of one repeatable object action, but every result sends him back into another reversal.

phases.observableAction: Bo sets the conker into the satchel, gathers himself, and moves toward the open doorway with careful, contained steps.
At the threshold Bo locks in place, then retreats and repeatedly transfers the conker between his paws and the satchel.
Each reversal leaves his shoulders higher, paws less neat, and grip tighter around the conker.
Bo ends clutching the conker close, with the satchel open and the doorway still visible beyond him.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The threshold stops Bo’s forward motion; retreat puts him back at the satchel, where each conker placement or removal creates the next opposite action until the object is gripped rather than placed.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: A tidy departure attempt becomes a self-tightening object loop, then breaks into visible distress.
contract.requiredLanding: Bo must finish with the conker held too tightly against himself, the satchel unresolved, and the doorway still spatially clear.
contract.performanceFreedom: The exact path of the scurry, number of tiny paw adjustments, tail counterbalance, and breath pattern may vary, but the conker state changes must remain unmistakable.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s worry and curiosity pull him into quick, sincere, object-focused behaviour; his tail and paws reveal what he cannot settle.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants the conker to make the outside step feel decided and safe.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: When the doorway confronts him, he freezes, retreats, and overcommits to the repeated object action.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Light squirrel steps, abrupt stop, paws gathering the conker carefully at first and clutching it by the end, tail balancing each reversal.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen under pressure would show a gulp and step through; Bo uniquely turns pressure into a fussy decision ritual around his satchel and conker.

comedyStaging.staysVisible: The conker, Bo’s paws, the lunch satchel and the open doorway remain readable in relation to one another so the audience tracks the decision loop and the pressure of the exit.
comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: Each conker move has small tactile weight: paw pads gather it, set it down or pull it back; the satchel shifts only when Bo actually touches or bumps it, proving the room is responding to his fussy momentum.
comedyStaging.payoffShape: A repeated in-out pattern tightens into faster, less tidy reversals until Bo’s body freezes and the final line pops out as the ritual fails him.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the conker into a magical chooser or animated character.
Do not make the loop so fast that the audience loses where the doorway is.
Do not cut away from the conker’s final position before Bo’s panic lands.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Keen enters with gentle curiosity; Bo’s body reacts before his social self can tidy it up.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Keen appears as a soft presence at the doorway: he taps lightly, peeks in, and keeps his weight outside the room’s center. Bo jolts before he can compose himself; the conker pops free, bounces through several fumbled catches, and ends hugged tight as Bo checks the object and then Keen.

contract.playableIntention: Keen offers entry as gently as possible; Bo’s body reveals how sealed and overwound the private loop has become.

phases.observableAction: Keen holds at the threshold, taps softly on the hollow, and peeks in without crossing into the room.
Bo jumps, launching the conker upward, then fumbles it through several catches before trapping it against his body.
Bo’s eyes snap from the hugged conker to Keen, measuring the object loss and the new witness in one quick check.
Keen remains calmly at the doorway with soft posture and no forward step after Bo’s startle.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s soft doorway knock interrupts the private loop; Bo’s startle sends the conker into the air, forcing a messy recovery, and Keen’s stillness prevents the interruption from becoming a chase into the room.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo’s private control becomes witnessed exposure, but Keen’s body language keeps the encounter gentle.
contract.requiredLanding: Bo must end hugging the conker inside the hollow while Keen waits at the threshold, leaving space between them.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow play in the conker’s arc, Bo’s fumble pattern, and Keen’s micro-softening, provided the startle is Bo’s oversize response and Keen does not crowd him.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Keen is forward and curious, but real courage for him includes softness before action rather than fearless pushing.
characterTruths.playableWant: Keen wants to make contact without startling the room more than necessary.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: At the threshold, he reduces his usual momentum into a light knock, a small lean, and a patient wait.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Forward interest contained in soft knees, open chest, gentle peek, and no uninvited step inside.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Bo would retreat into objects at this doorway; Keen uniquely brings brave curiosity while choosing restraint.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s squirrel body reacts fast; worry shows before he can tidy it into words.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants to recover the conker and regain a little control in front of the newcomer.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He springs, fumbles, then protects the object against his chest.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Quick vertical jolt, nimble but messy paw catches, tight hug of the conker, rapid eyeline from object to visitor.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would likely convert the mishap into forward engagement; Bo’s specific response is to clutch the decision object and stay deeper inside.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Bo’s shame becomes visible through attempts to control the tail; Keen’s awe must be still, sincere, and unshowy.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Bo’s words spill faster than his body can manage: he clutches near the conker, then turns inward as his tail suddenly expands and takes over the room. He grabs at it, trying to compress it back down, but the second expansion defeats the tidy effort. Keen stays still and openly impressed; Bo’s grip loosens, his shoulders drop, and he looks back with cautious disbelief rather than immediate confidence.

contract.playableIntention: Bo expects visible difference to cost him safety; Keen’s sincere stillness gives that visible difference a new possible meaning.

phases.observableAction: Bo leans forward with the conker close, paws tight and speech-driven motion spilling out faster than his posture can organize.
Bo’s tail expands suddenly; he grabs it with both paws, tries to hold it down, and is pulled off balance when it expands again.
Keen looks directly at the enlarged tail with widened eyes, lifted face, and still body, showing delight rather than alarm.
Bo stops fighting as hard, loosens his grip on the tail, lowers his shoulders, and checks Keen’s face with a small uncertain look.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Bo’s body tightens around the exposed worry; the tail expands beyond his hands, forcing the frame and his balance wider, and Keen’s still delighted gaze interrupts Bo’s attempt to hide it.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: The enlarged tail changes from something Bo is wrestling to something he cautiously allows to be seen.
contract.requiredLanding: Bo must end beside the enlarged tail with a softened grip and a questioning look toward Keen, not fully cured or hidden.
contract.performanceFreedom: The tail’s exact bounce, Bo’s paw placement, and Keen’s facial micro-reaction may vary, but the second expansion must clearly overpower Bo’s control and Keen must read sincere before Bo softens.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s large fluffy tail is an emotional and movement anchor; under worry, paws pull close and the tail tells the truth bigger than his face.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants to make his tail small and socially manageable in front of the witness.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He pleads physically with the tail by grabbing, squeezing, and trying to contain it, then pauses when the witness does not recoil.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Tight paws on tail fur, off-balance squirrel posture, shoulders lifted then dropping, eyeline checking Keen before trusting the moment.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen’s pressure tell is a gulp before a step; Bo’s canon tail makes the feeling physically larger than his control, so another character could not carry this beat.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Keen’s courage is bright, curious, and relationship-forward, with action guided by visible feeling rather than swagger.
characterTruths.playableWant: Keen wants Bo to know the tail can be looked at with delight, without turning Bo into a target.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He holds still instead of charging in, letting his impressed gaze arrive before any movement toward Bo.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Open face, widened eyes, lifted chin, body quiet at the threshold, no grab for the tail and no laugh at Bo.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: A deadpan or fixer character could make the tail a joke or a problem; Keen uniquely reframes it through eager, sincere wonder.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Keen offers silliness as care; Bo’s smile grows cautiously and his movement out stays modest, with some fear still carried in the body.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Keen redirects attention onto his own tail with a gentle turn and a small wiggle, offering himself as the harmless comparison while keeping the moment soft. Bo studies Keen’s tail, then his own; his grip releases, the conker is set down without ceremony, and his tail slowly deflates. Bo’s smile grows only enough for the next step, then his tail lifts the satchel and he moves out with Keen, leaving the conker behind.

contract.playableIntention: Keen makes himself the safe silly object so Bo can stop being the spectacle and choose one small accompanied step.

phases.observableAction: Keen turns his body to present his own tail, keeping the movement light and non-demanding.
Keen gives a small wiggle while his tail remains limp and unresponsive, then holds the result without pushing for applause.
Bo looks from Keen’s tail to his own, loosens his hold, sets the conker down near the satchel area, and lets his tail deflate gradually.
The conker rests inside the warm hollow as Bo and Keen move toward the doorway together, with Bo’s tail carrying the satchel.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s self-directed demonstration moves the focus off Bo; Bo compares the two tails, releases the conker, and the softened tail becomes useful by lifting the satchel as the pair leave the room.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo changes from guarding the conker and tail to leaving the conker behind and allowing the tail to help him move.
contract.requiredLanding: The final image must read as Bo and Keen exiting together while the conker remains inside as the abandoned decision tool.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow gentle variation in Keen’s wiggle, Bo’s smile size, tail deflation speed, and exit cadence, as long as Bo remains modest rather than suddenly fearless.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Keen is kinetic and brave, but his best courage includes making himself available and a little vulnerable for someone else.
characterTruths.playableWant: Keen wants to lower the stakes by putting the harmless joke on himself.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He softens his usual forward energy into a small offered demonstration and waits for Bo to process it.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Loose turn, light wiggle, open posture, no demand for a big reaction, then an easy path toward the doorway.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Bo would make the comparison private and worried; Keen uniquely uses his forward courage to offer self-exposure as kindness.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s worry shows through small paws, quick comparison looks, and a tail that carries emotion as well as movement.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants enough safety to take one outward step without needing the conker to decide for him.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He studies before moving, releases the object carefully, lets the tail soften, and accepts movement without becoming showy.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Look from Keen’s tail to his own, paw unclenching, quiet conker set-down, cautious smile, tail lifting the satchel as he exits.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would turn relief into immediate momentum; Bo’s release is squirrel-small, object-specific, and cautious enough to preserve the remaining ache.

camera.storyPointOfView: Bo’s private delay ritual, with the world outside present only as voice and doorway pressure.
camera.emotionalDistanceStart: Near and protective, sharing the scale of the objects Bo trusts.
camera.emotionalDistanceEnd: Still near, but with the doorway feeling larger because he has not crossed it.
camera.revealStrategy: Reveal the problem indirectly: the door is visible before Bo admits anything is wrong.
camera.shotScale: Intimate interior object-led medium-close scale, not a room master.
camera.lensIntent: A close, child-height relationship that makes the conker and satchel feel consequential while keeping the doorway readable in depth.
camera.cameraHeight: Low to the hollow floor, aligned with Bo’s hands and decision objects.
camera.composition: Foreground conker and satchel anchor the frame; Bo occupies the warm middle of the hollow; the open door interrupts the curve of the room behind him.
camera.depthStrategy: Depth is pressure: manageable objects in front, Bo in the middle, outside day waiting behind.
camera.cameraBehavior: Still enough to feel domestic, with tiny hesitant adjustments following Bo’s attention back to the conker instead of toward the door.
camera.focusStrategy: Hold the conker and satchel sharp with Bo, allowing the doorway to remain legible but slightly less graspable until Mum’s voice makes it active.
camera.lightingFunction: Honeyed interior warmth protects Bo while doorway light quietly asks for forward motion.
camera.paletteFunction: Warm browns and golds enclose the room; the exterior light carries a cooler, larger note without becoming hostile.
camera.performanceVisibility: Hands, eyeline, and small retractions must be readable; do not bury the delay in broad facial fear.
camera.editorialPurpose: Start the sequence from inside the ritual so later interruptions feel like changes to Bo’s private system.
camera.memorableLandingImage: Bo in the warm hollow with the decision objects close and the doorway still unanswered.
camera.providerInstruction: Start low inside the hollow across the conker and satchel toward Bo, keep the open doorway readable in bright depth, and let Bo’s small paw hesitations carry the delay as Mum’s offscreen call turns the room into a question.

stages.purpose: Turn the hollow oak from cosy safety into the first little delaying chamber.
stages.primaryEvent: Mum’s offscreen call activates the open doorway, and Bo answers by staying with the conker and satchel instead of moving toward the threshold.
stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: The room stops being only comforting; Bo’s promised minute reveals itself as a way to keep the decision reversible.
stages.cameraAndTransition: Begin embedded with Bo’s controllable objects, then let the bright doorway sit in depth as a pressure he keeps not choosing.
stages.observableEndState: Bo remains inside beside the satchel and conker, with the open doorway visibly waiting beyond him.

camera.storyPointOfView: Bo’s worry as it tries to turn a giant social fear into a small repeatable object action.

camera.providerInstruction: Track the conker’s in-out-in-out journey between Bo’s paws and the satchel while keeping the open doorway spatially present; let the frame tighten only as Bo’s tidy decision ritual breaks into panic.

camera.lightingFunction: Doorway light stays constant but reads differently because Bo approaches it with Keen.
camera.paletteFunction: Interior warmth remains as a trace of safety; exterior light adds openness without washing away the worry.
camera.performanceVisibility: Keen’s gentle self-joke, Bo’s cautious almost-smile, conker release, tail deflation, and modest exit must all read clearly.
camera.editorialPurpose: Convert the scene turn into a small actionable step while preserving bittersweet residue.
camera.memorableLandingImage: The conker left inside as Bo and Keen move out together.
camera.providerInstruction: Frame Keen’s still-tail demonstration gently, then make Bo’s conker release and tail softening visible before holding from inside the hollow as Bo and Keen move toward the doorway with the conker clearly left behind.

stages.purpose: Release the held vulnerability through Keen making himself the safe silly object.
stages.primaryEvent: Keen offers his own tail as comparison, turns and wiggles, and his tail remains completely still.
stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: The joke moves away from Bo; Keen chooses harmless self-exposure.
stages.cameraAndTransition: Cut to a threshold-shared setup that treats Keen’s demonstration as generous silliness, not a performance demanding applause.
stages.observableEndState: Keen has demonstrated a tail that does nothing, with Bo watching rather than hiding.

stages.purpose: Make Bo’s old decision machine visibly lose its job.
stages.primaryEvent: Bo looks from Keen’s tail to his own; his grip relaxes, the conker is set down in the warm room near the satchel, and his tail slowly deflates as an almost-smile appears.
stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: Relief enters, but not as a cure; the conker no longer has to decide for him.
stages.cameraAndTransition: Let the eye follow Bo’s comparison from Keen’s tail to his own, then down to the conker’s final placement before returning to Bo’s almost-smile.
stages.observableEndState: The conker rests on the hollow floor behind Bo’s next choice, while Bo’s tail has softened.

stages.purpose: Turn the doorway from test into shared movement while preserving the ache.
stages.primaryEvent: Keen offers a walk for fresh air; Bo’s smile grows enough to agree, his tail picks up the bag, and Bo walks out with Keen, leaving the conker behind.
stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: Bo chooses one small step with a witness, not a solved life.
stages.cameraAndTransition: Hold the room-door relationship as both move toward the same opening, then let the conker remain visible in the warm interior foreground.
stages.observableEndState: Bo and Keen are moving through the doorway together, with the conker left behind inside.

internalShots.purpose: Reset tension into a gentle laugh by making Keen the object of the comparison.
internalShots.framingAndCamera: Shared threshold view angled so Keen’s turn and Bo’s watchful reaction both read without becoming a safe two-shot pattern.
internalShots.storyAction: Keen says, “Mine does nothing. Watch,” turns, wiggles, and his tail hangs still; he adds, “See? Nothing.”
internalShots.performanceFocus: Keen’s silliness is offered softly; Bo watches for whether this is kindness or another risk.
internalShots.landingImage: Keen finished with the harmless demonstration while Bo remains present enough to look.
internalShots.cutReason: New comic mechanism: from awe at Bo’s tail to Keen’s self-joke.

internalShots.purpose: Make Bo’s release physical and clarify the conker payoff.
internalShots.framingAndCamera: Object-aware interior view following Bo’s gaze to his tail and down to the conker as it is placed behind the choice to leave.
internalShots.storyAction: Bo looks at Keen’s tail, then at his own; his tail deflates gradually, his grip loosens, and the conker comes to rest near the satchel in the warm room.
internalShots.performanceFocus: The almost-smile is cautious; the conker release is not a discard with triumph, just a decision machine becoming unnecessary.
internalShots.landingImage: The conker resting inside the hollow while Bo’s softened tail and small smile show one notch of ease.
internalShots.cutReason: New information and motif payoff: the conker’s final placement must be unmistakable before the exit.

internalShots.purpose: Land the doorway rhyme as modest shared movement.

internalShots.performanceFocus: Bo’s agreement is a small brave exhale; his body still carries caution even as it moves.
internalShots.landingImage: Bo and Keen crossing toward the outside light together, the conker left behind in the warm room.
internalShots.cutReason: Final landing view; no further internal cut because the image of shared movement and abandoned decision switch is the scene’s payoff.

performances.speaker: Bo's Mum
performances.exactDialogue: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
performances.voiceIdentity: Offscreen Mum: warm household steadiness, practical but listening for Bo’s hesitation; not scolding, not sugary.
performances.dramaticIntention: Nudge Bo toward the doorway while keeping the morning ordinary enough that he can step into it.
performances.subtext: I know this is big, so I’m making it sound like a normal leaving-the-house moment.
performances.relationshipTarget: Bo, from another room, close enough to care but giving him space.
performances.emotionalEntry: Busy morning warmth with a faint check-in underneath.
performances.emotionalExit: Hopeful that the gentle prompt will move him, but leaving room for his reply.
performances.pace: Unhurried domestic call; soften slightly on the question mark after Learning Circle.
performances.rhythm: Two-part call: first the real nudge, then the everyday lunch reminder as emotional cover.
performances.pauses: Tiny settling pause after “BO,” so it is a loving call-in, not a bark; brief lift before “Don’t forget” to make the lunch tag feel practical.
performances.breaths: Small breath before the second sentence, like she is moving through the house while speaking.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Heard offscreen; her voice creates the doorway pressure that makes Bo glance over, then shrink back to the conker.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: [quietly] BO, it’s TIME for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your LUNCH.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Her calm voice contrasts Bo’s tiny, controlled body; the ordinariness of her delivery makes his stillness read louder.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin after Bo’s paws hover over the objects; let the line arrive from offscreen, then leave a beat for his glance toward the doorway.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.exactDialogue: I’ll go in a minute Mum.
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: small, careful, self-managing; tries to sound reasonable while his breath betrays the pressure.
performances.dramaticIntention: Buy time from Mum without letting her hear how stuck he is.
performances.subtext: If I say it tidily, maybe I can stay in this safe little circle a bit longer.
performances.relationshipTarget: Bo’s Mum offscreen, with the conker as his safer secondary listener.
performances.emotionalEntry: Startled by the prompt, shrinking back toward control.
performances.emotionalExit: Momentarily relieved, but more attached to the conker than before.
performances.pace: Soft and contained; slightly too quick on “I’ll go,” then slow on “in a minute.”
performances.rhythm: A neat little sentence trying to behave; the final “Mum” asks not to be pushed.
performances.pauses: No big pause inside the line; the hesitation belongs before it as his glance retracts from the doorway.
performances.breaths: Tiny inhale before “I’ll,” held shallow through the line.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Paws hover, retract, then return toward the conker as he answers.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: [nervous] I’ll go in a MINUTE Mum.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice performs compliance while the body chooses the objects; the mismatch reveals the fear without naming it.
performances.expectedTiming: Do not start on the offscreen cue. Let Bo glance toward the doorway, hover a paw, then answer as he pulls back.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.exactDialogue: Maybe, I’ll go tomorrow instead. Tomorrow sounds much better than today. Tomorrow everything will OK, not today.
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: anxious logic-maker; treating each thought like a careful conker placement that might make the day safe.
performances.dramaticIntention: Convince himself more than anyone else that postponing is sensible, not fear.
performances.subtext: Tomorrow is imaginary, so tomorrow can’t hurt me.
performances.relationshipTarget: Mostly himself and the conker; Mum is distant in his mind, the doorway is the threat.
performances.emotionalEntry: Trying to convert worry into a tidy plan.
performances.emotionalExit: Less tidy; the repetition comforts him but also winds him tighter.
performances.pace: Begins measured and sincere; gently gathers speed as the ritual starts to take over.
performances.rhythm: Circular, self-soothing repetition: “Tomorrow” keeps returning like the conker loop.
performances.pauses: Small thinking pause after “Maybe,”; cleaner sentence break after “instead”; final comma before “not today” should feel like a little retreat.
performances.breaths: Breath in before “Maybe,” as he places the conker; shorter breath before each new “Tomorrow.”
performances.nonVerbalActions: Conker placement is still precise at first; voice should sound like he is arranging facts in a row.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: Maybe, I’ll go TOMORROW instead. Tomorrow sounds much BETTER than today. Tomorrow everything will OK, [pause] NOT today.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice and body share the same ritual logic: if the words are placed correctly, maybe the threshold can be avoided.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin during the first careful placement, before his real approach to the door; allow the final “not today” to land as he reorients away from the threshold.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: brave in miniature; the tiniest experiment in hope.
performances.dramaticIntention: Dare himself one step closer to the door.
performances.subtext: Maybe I can do this if I only touch the thought lightly.
performances.relationshipTarget: Himself, with the doorway now pulling his focus.
performances.emotionalEntry: A small opening after the postponement ritual.
performances.emotionalExit: Suspended at the threshold; hope is present but fragile.
performances.pace: Very gentle, tentative, slightly slower than his previous line.
performances.rhythm: One careful step of sound, not a declaration.
performances.pauses: A faint pre-line pause as his momentum reaches the door; no internal pause.
performances.breaths: Small hopeful inhale, almost a held breath through “OK.”
performances.nonVerbalActions: He makes the first real approach to the open door; body still compact but moving.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice offers the forward step the body is trying to take; both are tentative, neither triumphant.
performances.expectedTiming: Land after the measured conker placement and as he approaches the threshold; leave room afterward for the freeze.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: the control finally cracks, but still child-small rather than broadly frantic.
performances.dramaticIntention: Pull himself back from the risk before the doorway can swallow him.
performances.subtext: The tiny brave thought opened a huge trapdoor.
performances.relationshipTarget: Himself and the threshold; the room is suddenly the only safe listener.
performances.emotionalEntry: Frozen at the threshold, breath caught.
performances.emotionalExit: Snapped back into ritual, clinging harder to the conker.
performances.pace: Quick burst after the held threshold freeze.
performances.rhythm: Broken, sprung release: one panic-thought escaping before he scurries back.
performances.pauses: Hold silence before the line long enough for the breath to catch; no pause inside.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Momentum stops at the threshold, then the line fires and sends him back into the conker loop.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The gasp is the threshold freeze becoming sound; the line justifies the sudden scurry back without making him cartoon-hysterical.
performances.expectedTiming: After the threshold freeze, not on arrival; line should trigger the first accelerated return into the room.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: gentle, open, curious; careful not to fill the room too much.
performances.dramaticIntention: Make Bo feel safe by entering as a friendly visitor, not a rescuer.
performances.subtext: I’m here, but I won’t come closer than you can handle.
performances.relationshipTarget: Bo, from the doorway, after a respectful knock.
performances.emotionalEntry: Soft curiosity, reading the room before speaking.
performances.emotionalExit: Still welcoming, ready to wait through Bo’s startle.
performances.pace: Light, friendly, not bouncy; leave air around the greeting.
performances.rhythm: Tiny knock-breath, then a simple introduction with a smile in it.
performances.pauses: Let the knock breathe before the line; a small pause after “Hi!”
performances.breaths: Easy inhale before “Hi,” quiet enough to keep the room calm.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen taps lightly and peeks in, keeping weight outside the room’s center.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: His restrained volume matches his body staying at the doorway; the friendliness is offered, not pushed.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin only after the light tap has landed and Bo has a fraction of a second to register a presence.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.exactDialogue: Aida sent me. She thought we should meet.
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: matter-of-fact kindness; lets Aida’s name do the reassuring, not overexplaining.
performances.dramaticIntention: Give Bo a reason to trust the visit without demanding trust from him.
performances.subtext: Someone who knows both of us thought this might help, but you still get to choose.
performances.relationshipTarget: Bo, who has just startled and is protecting the conker.
performances.emotionalEntry: Gentle after the introduction, noticing Bo’s fumble without commenting on it.
performances.emotionalExit: Patient invitation; no pressure to answer quickly.
performances.pace: Calm, evenly spaced; slow down a touch on “meet.”
performances.rhythm: Two soft facts, each with its own landing.
performances.pauses: Brief reassuring pause after “me.”; no dramatic weight, just space.
performances.breaths: Small breath before the second sentence as Keen checks Bo’s reaction.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen remains outside the center, still enough to prove he is not advancing while Bo gathers the conker.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: AIDA sent me. She thought we should MEET.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice’s patience supports Keen’s stillness; Bo’s fumble remains comic because Keen does not pounce on it.
performances.expectedTiming: After Bo’s conker fumble has resolved into a tight hug; deliver while Keen stays at the doorway.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.exactDialogue: What if nobody likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: social self trying to confess neatly, but fear outruns his tidy manners.
performances.dramaticIntention: Get Keen to understand the real danger without having to be looked at too closely.
performances.subtext: If you know the embarrassing part and don’t laugh, maybe I can breathe.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, though Bo keeps checking the conker and his own body for safety.
performances.emotionalEntry: Embarrassed, freshly startled, trying to recover composure.
performances.emotionalExit: Exposed; the named fear invites the tail to betray him.
performances.pace: Begins fast but intelligible; second sentence drops lower; final question tightens toward “THING.”
performances.rhythm: Spilling confession: worry, retreat, then the forbidden word.
performances.pauses: Tiny breath-gap after the first question; heavier drop before “What if my tail” as he debates saying it.
performances.breaths: Shallow, quick breath before “I don’t think”; little gulp before “THING.”
performances.nonVerbalActions: Words spill as he clutches near the conker and turns inward; tail pressure begins to build underneath the line.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: [nervous] What if NOBODY likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice tries to contain the confession while the body can’t; the line should feel like it accidentally summons the tail expansion.
performances.expectedTiming: Start as Bo clutches near the conker; let “THING” land just before or into the tail’s first soft burst.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.exactDialogue: Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: pleading with his own body as if manners might make it obey.
performances.dramaticIntention: Make the tail stop embarrassing him in front of Keen.
performances.subtext: Please don’t show him the part of me I can’t control.
performances.relationshipTarget: His tail first, Keen second as the witness he is ashamed of.
performances.emotionalExit: Defeated by the second expansion, less able to hide.
performances.pace: First phrase pops out; second phrase is pleading, squeezed, slightly longer.
performances.rhythm: Command breaks into please; control collapses into begging.
performances.pauses: Sharp beat after “Stop it!” as he grabs at the tail; no pause after “Please” because the plea tumbles out.
performances.breaths: Breath is tight and high; a tiny strain through “normal tail.”
performances.nonVerbalActions: He grabs at the expanded tail and tries to compress it down; the second expansion defeats the effort.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: Stop it! [pause] PLEASE just be a NORMAL TAIL!
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The pause is the physical grab; the plea should sound squeezed by the effort to compress the tail.
performances.expectedTiming: “Stop it!” lands on the first grab; “Please just be a normal tail!” rides the failed compression into the second burst.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: sincere awe without performance; stillness makes the compliment land as truth, not rescue.
performances.dramaticIntention: Change what Bo thinks is embarrassing into something worth looking at.
performances.subtext: I see the thing you’re scared of, and I’m not scared or laughing.
performances.relationshipTarget: Bo, specifically the ashamed part of Bo that expects rejection.
performances.emotionalEntry: Quietly impressed, taking in the tail before speaking.
performances.emotionalExit: Open admiration, leaving space for Bo to believe it.
performances.pace: Slow and still; “Whoa” is breathed in, not shouted; “AMAZING” lands with simple certainty.
performances.rhythm: Awe, then the plain truth of the compliment.
performances.pauses: Meaningful pause after “Whoa.” so Bo can feel Keen actually looking.
performances.breaths: Soft inhale before “Whoa,” like surprise turning into wonder.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen stays still and openly impressed; no pointing, no big reaction.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice’s stillness redirects the room; it must not compete with the tail’s size, only witness it.
performances.expectedTiming: Hold Keen’s silent reaction first; speak after the tail has completed its follow-through and Bo is braced for judgment.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: disbelief with the smallest opening toward being seen kindly.
performances.dramaticIntention: Ask Keen to confirm it without making Bo risk fully believing him yet.
performances.subtext: Please mean that. Please don’t take it back.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, now safer than the conker for one fragile second.
performances.emotionalEntry: Ashamed and braced, grip loosening after unexpected praise.
performances.emotionalExit: Cautious hope; shoulders drop a little.
performances.pace: Very soft and slow; the line almost doesn’t dare exist.
performances.rhythm: The ellipsis is the thought crossing from shame to possibility.
performances.pauses: Honor the leading ellipsis with a real pre-line silence; slight lift at the end, not needy-big.
performances.breaths: Small exhale before “you,” as grip releases.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Bo’s grip loosens, shoulders drop, and he looks back with cautious disbelief.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice follows the body’s slow release; no immediate confidence, just the first unclenching.
performances.expectedTiming: After Keen’s compliment has had time to land; begin as Bo looks back rather than during the tail action.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: kind mischief; uses gentle self-silliness to take heat off Bo.
performances.dramaticIntention: Invite Bo to compare without feeling examined, by making Keen himself the harmless joke.
performances.subtext: You’re not the odd one out; I can be silly first.
performances.emotionalEntry: Encouraged by Bo’s tiny opening, careful not to over-celebrate.
performances.emotionalExit: Playfully vulnerable, setting up the still-tail gag.
performances.pace: Light and matter-of-fact; don’t oversell the joke.
performances.rhythm: Simple setup, then a tiny showman’s beat on “Watch.”
performances.pauses: Brief pause before “Watch.” as he turns to present his own tail.
performances.breaths: Small smile-breath before the line; no laugh tag, let the body carry the gag.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen redirects attention onto his own tail with a gentle turn and small wiggle.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice stays modest so the physical still-tail gag has room to be funny.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin as Keen starts the gentle turn; “Watch” lands just before the wiggle attempt.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: warmly deadpan; proud of the failure because it helps Bo.
performances.dramaticIntention: Turn comparison into relief by making “nothing” safe and funny.
performances.subtext: My tail’s boring, and that is completely allowed too.
performances.relationshipTarget: Bo, inviting a smile without demanding one.
performances.emotionalEntry: After the clean still-tail pause, lightly amused at himself.
performances.emotionalExit: Softened room; ready to offer the next gentle step outside.
performances.pace: Dry, small, with a clean comic landing.
performances.rhythm: Let the visual nothing happen first; then tag it simply.
performances.pauses: Must follow a clean silent beat after the wiggle; tiny pause after “See?”
performances.breaths: Easy breath after the failed wiggle, like he’s perfectly content with the result.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen’s tail does nothing; the gag is held before he comments.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The line is the button on the stillness, not the joke itself; keep it underplayed.
performances.expectedTiming: Only after the still-tail gag has clearly landed and Bo has had time to study it.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.exactDialogue: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: gentle practical optimism; care disguised as an ordinary walk.
performances.dramaticIntention: Offer Bo a next step that is smaller than “Learning Circle” and therefore possible.
performances.subtext: We don’t have to solve today; we can just move together for a little bit.
performances.relationshipTarget: Bo, whose body still carries some fear.
performances.emotionalEntry: Room softened by the joke, Bo almost ready but not fully confident.
performances.pace: Calm and inviting; second sentence reassuring but not preachy.
performances.rhythm: First sentence opens the door; second sentence cushions the step.
performances.pauses: Small pause between sentences; leave a little space after “walk” if Bo is watching the doorway.
performances.breaths: Easy breath before “Fresh air,” as if the idea itself makes the room bigger.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen keeps the offer soft, allowing Bo to look, loosen, set the conker down, and let the tail deflate in stages.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: Let’s go for a WALK and get some FRESH AIR. Fresh air always HELPS.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice creates a modest path out, matching Bo’s staged release rather than rushing him into bravery.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin after Bo has reacted to the still-tail gag; allow the line to cover the first stage of Bo’s loosening, not the final exit.

performances.speaker: Bo
performances.voiceIdentity: Bo: cautious relief; not fixed, just willing to take the next small step.
performances.dramaticIntention: Accept Keen’s offer without pretending the fear has disappeared.
performances.subtext: I can try this if it stays this gentle.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, with one last private goodbye to the conker as safety object.
performances.emotionalEntry: Softened by being witnessed and by Keen’s harmless silliness.
performances.emotionalExit: Small readiness; fear still carried, but moving.
performances.pace: Slow, shy, with a tiny warmth blooming on “nice.”
performances.rhythm: One careful agreement; the smile arrives late.
performances.pauses: Pre-line pause as Bo looks from Keen’s tail to his own, then to the conker; no internal pause.
performances.breaths: Quiet release-breath before “That,” like the grip has finally let go.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Bo studies, loosens, sets the conker down without ceremony, tail softens, then he moves out with Keen as the satchel lifts.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: The exhale is the physical release of the conker and the tail’s softening; voice remains modest so the fear is not magically erased.
performances.expectedTiming: After the staged release has begun: look, loosen, set down; let “nice” coincide with the almost-smile before the modest move toward the doorway.

shots.openingImage: Bo inside the hollow oak beside the lunch satchel and conker, with the open doorway brighter behind him like an unanswered question.
