shots.openingImage: Bo’s paw sets the conker into the satchel while the open doorway waits just ahead.
shots.referenceRoles: Bo’s reference anchors identity, paw behavior, and tail counterbalance. The hollow-oak scene look anchors the unchanged warm interior and threshold light. The conker and satchel are the continuity anchors for the decision loop; they must remain spatially related to the doorway.

shots.openingImage: The open doorway from inside the hollow as a soft shadow touches its edge.
shots.referenceRoles: Bo and Keen character references anchor identity and contrasting behavior: Bo’s quick squirrel startle against Keen’s contained forward curiosity. The hollow-oak look owns the doorway/interior light relationship. The conker is the comic continuity prop that proves Bo’s private system has been interrupted.

shots.openingImage: Bo inside the hollow clutching the conker, angled toward Keen at the doorway as the private fear is about to spill out.
shots.referenceRoles: Bo’s reference anchors the tail as his emotional and movement tell; Keen’s reference anchors bright curiosity made gentle. The hollow-oak scene look anchors warm interior continuity and the doorway witness position. The conker remains present but the tail becomes the truthful visual motif in this shot.

shots.openingImage: Keen at the threshold turned slightly toward Bo, ready to make his own tail the demonstration.
shots.referenceRoles: Bo and Keen references anchor identity, tail behavior, and the contrast between Bo’s cautious release and Keen’s offered silliness. The hollow-oak scene look anchors the warm-room foreground and constant doorway light. The conker, satchel, and Bo’s tail are the motif/payoff objects: conker abandoned, satchel carried by the softened tail.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn the hollow oak from cosy safety into the first little delaying chamber.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Mum’s offscreen call activates the open doorway, and Bo answers by staying with the conker and satchel instead of moving toward the threshold.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The room stops being only comforting; Bo’s promised minute reveals itself as a way to keep the decision reversible.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin embedded with Bo’s controllable objects, then let the bright doorway sit in depth as a pressure he keeps not choosing.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo remains inside beside the satchel and conker, with the open doorway visibly waiting beyond him.

coverage.purpose: Put the audience inside Bo’s private delay ritual before the room tightens.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Low, close interior view across the conker and lunch satchel toward Bo, with the open doorway held farther back as a bright vertical interruption.
coverage.storyAction: Mum calls from outside; Bo looks between the objects and the door, answers, “I’ll go in a minute Mum,” then quietly extends the delay by treating the conker as his listener.
coverage.performanceFocus: Small-choice panic: paws hover near the satchel, attention flicks to the doorway, then returns to the conker for safety.
coverage.landingImage: Bo still inside the hollow with the conker and satchel close, the doorway unanswered in the background.
coverage.cutReason: No internal cut; the one idea is the room becoming Bo’s delay machine.

units.closingImage: Bo remains beside the conker and satchel while the open doorway holds its place in the room.

stagePlan.purpose: Make the doorway too large for Bo’s current courage.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo places the conker in the bag and reaches the open door, but the threshold freezes him and sends him back toward tomorrow.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The first real attempt to leave collapses into retreat.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to the threshold already looming in the frame, then let the camera stop with Bo when his body stops.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo is frozen at the open door, unable to step through.

stagePlan.purpose: Convert retreat into the conker decision-game.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo scurries back inside, takes the conker out, then talks himself toward today and puts it back into the bag.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: A tiny hopeful verdict appears: today could be manageable.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Follow the conker’s path back from the bag to Bo’s paws and back again, keeping the doorway in relation so the audience tracks the loop.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The conker is back in the bag and Bo has briefly recommitted to today.

stagePlan.purpose: Let the game turn into a panic machine.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo’s anxiety rises again, he pulls the conker out once more, and the final question bursts through the ritual.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The joke of the switch flips into vulnerability; deciding harder makes him less in control.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Tighten around Bo, conker, satchel, and doorway without losing geography, ending on the conker held too tightly.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo clutches the conker with visible panic, the satchel and doorway still unresolved.

coverage.purpose: Give the door its first physical victory over Bo.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Threshold-facing view from inside the hollow, close enough that Bo’s stop feels bodily rather than scenic.
coverage.storyAction: Bo puts the conker in the bag, approaches the open door, opens it, freezes, and begins bargaining for tomorrow.
coverage.performanceFocus: The body reaches commitment and then locks: breath caught, paws pulled close, momentum gone.
coverage.landingImage: Bo stopped at the open doorway with the bag near him and no step taken outside.
coverage.cutReason: Changed emotional state and scale of pressure: the doorway is no longer background, it is the obstacle.

coverage.purpose: Make the conker physically operate as the decision switch.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Object-led view at satchel height, travelling only enough to follow conker in, conker out, conker in while the doorway remains spatially readable.
coverage.storyAction: Bo retreats, removes the conker, admits today could be possible, sighs, and puts the conker back.
coverage.performanceFocus: Fussy overcommitment: careful hands try to make the tiny object produce certainty.
coverage.landingImage: The conker sits inside the satchel as Bo briefly steadies himself.
coverage.cutReason: New visual idea: the argument transfers from doorway to object loop.

coverage.purpose: Let the loop fail and expose the panic underneath.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Closer on Bo with the conker held between him and the open-room depth; the frame has less breathing room than before.
coverage.storyAction: The thought that today might not be okay returns; Bo pulls the conker out again and asks, “What if it’s not OK?!”
coverage.performanceFocus: Control frays: the paws stop being tidy, the conker is gripped instead of placed, and the line breaks the rhythm.
coverage.landingImage: Bo clutching the conker while the bag and open doorway remain unfinished business.
coverage.cutReason: The final panic beat earns a fresh boundary because the next event is an outside presence interrupting the private loop.

units.closingImage: Bo holds the conker close against himself, with the satchel open and the doorway still visible beyond.

stagePlan.purpose: Introduce Keen as a gentle interruption rather than an invasion.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: A shadow reaches the doorway, Keen gently taps on the hollow tree and peeks inside, changing the private room into a shared threshold.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The outside world arrives softly, but it still arrives.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to the doorway from Bo’s interior perspective, discovering Keen only when the room does.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Keen is present at the doorway, paused and not pushing in.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn Bo’s private control into visible startle without making Keen unsafe.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo jumps, the conker flies, he catches and fumbles it into a hug, then looks from the conker to Keen as Keen explains Aida sent him.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The startle is funny, but the softness of Keen’s delivery keeps it from becoming humiliation.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Let the conker’s flight briefly lead the eye, then settle into a shared threshold composition.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo hugs the conker inside the room while Keen remains gently at the doorway.

coverage.purpose: Make Keen’s entrance a discovered presence inside Bo’s point of view.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Interior view toward the doorway; the knock enters before the frame fully admits Keen, preserving Bo’s startle.
coverage.storyAction: A shadow appears, Keen taps a gentle shave-and-a-haircut knock, peeks in, holds a beat, and says, “Hi! I'm Keen.”
coverage.performanceFocus: Keen’s body stays soft and available; the knock behaves like it knows the room can be startled.
coverage.landingImage: Keen at the doorway with space between him and Bo’s interior.
coverage.cutReason: New information and altered privacy: another character now occupies the threshold.

coverage.purpose: Pay off the startle and show the conker losing authority.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Quick object-follow within the same unit as the conker pops up and Bo fumbles it, then settle to include Bo’s hug and Keen’s doorway position.
coverage.storyAction: Bo jumps, the conker flies, he catches it after several fumbles, hugs it, and immediately looks from it to Keen while Keen says, “Aida sent me. She thought we should meet.”
coverage.performanceFocus: Bo’s panic is in the overlarge recovery; Keen’s calm is in not advancing after the startle.
coverage.landingImage: Bo clutching the conker, Keen still outside the room’s center at the threshold.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes from entrance discovery to consequence of interruption; it is comic punctuation and altered power.

units.closingImage: Bo hugging the conker inside the hollow while Keen waits at the threshold.

stagePlan.purpose: Name the real social fear now that a safe witness is present.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo blurts that nobody may like him at the Learning Circle and fears his tail doing the thing, moving the problem from conker logic to being seen.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The private delay becomes an exposed belonging fear.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin close enough to catch the blurt as a spill, with Keen still held in the doorway relation rather than cut away as judgment.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo is visibly exposed in front of Keen, no longer hiding behind the conker game.

stagePlan.purpose: Force the feared truth into the room physically.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo’s tail suddenly poofs, he grabs and pleads with it, and it poofs larger again instead of obeying.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The thing he feared happens exactly when it matters; the room inhales.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Allow the tail movement to expand the frame and briefly disturb Bo’s attempt to stay small.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The enlarged tail is undeniable in the room, with Bo struggling against it.

stagePlan.purpose: Reframe shame through Keen’s sincere awe.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Keen stares impressed and says, “Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING,” causing Bo to pause his struggle, calm slightly, and ask, “…you think so?”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The tail changes from disaster to wonder for one fragile moment.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold after Keen’s awe so the turn can cross Bo’s face and body before the next gag releases it.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo is still with the tail, but his grip and face have softened into uncertain curiosity.

coverage.purpose: Let Bo’s fear come out as a spill rather than a neat explanation.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Close shared interior-threshold composition with Bo foregrounded and Keen present but not dominant.
coverage.storyAction: Bo blurts, “What if nobody likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?”
coverage.performanceFocus: Bo’s words outrun his tidiness; Keen listens without stepping in to solve.
coverage.landingImage: Bo exposed in the warm room with Keen still holding the threshold.
coverage.cutReason: New emotional information: the hidden fear is now spoken.

coverage.purpose: Make the tail’s uncontrolled truth bigger than Bo’s control system.
coverage.framingAndCamera: The frame widens or yields as the tail poofs, allowing its size to interrupt the previously tight room geometry.
coverage.storyAction: The tail poofs twice its size; Bo grabs it and says, “Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!” before it poofs larger again.
coverage.performanceFocus: Bo’s control fails physically: he tries to contain the tail as if politeness could make it obey.
coverage.landingImage: Bo wrapped up in the enlarged tail’s presence, unable to make it normal.
coverage.cutReason: Impact and new visual idea: the feared thing enters the frame and changes the scale of the room.

coverage.purpose: Let Keen’s wonder rewrite the meaning of what everyone is looking at.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Hold both the tail’s size and Keen’s face-line toward it, then settle on Bo’s softened response without rushing away.
coverage.storyAction: Keen looks impressed and says, “Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING.” Bo pauses, calms a little, and asks, “…you think so?”
coverage.performanceFocus: Keen’s still delight is the turn; Bo’s curiosity must arrive cautiously, not as instant confidence.
coverage.landingImage: Bo’s grip relaxed against the tail, looking toward Keen with fragile uncertainty.
coverage.cutReason: The hold is the point; no extra reaction cut is needed until the next unit changes the mechanism to Keen’s self-joke.

units.closingImage: Bo beside his enlarged tail with his grip loosened, looking toward Keen in uncertain calm.

stagePlan.purpose: Release the held vulnerability through Keen making himself the safe silly object.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Keen offers his own tail as comparison, turns and wiggles, and his tail remains completely still.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The joke moves away from Bo; Keen chooses harmless self-exposure.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to a threshold-shared setup that treats Keen’s demonstration as generous silliness, not a performance demanding applause.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Keen has demonstrated a tail that does nothing, with Bo watching rather than hiding.

stagePlan.purpose: Make Bo’s old decision machine visibly lose its job.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo looks from Keen’s tail to his own; his grip relaxes, the conker is set down in the warm room near the satchel, and his tail slowly deflates as an almost-smile appears.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Relief enters, but not as a cure; the conker no longer has to decide for him.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Let the eye follow Bo’s comparison from Keen’s tail to his own, then down to the conker’s final placement before returning to Bo’s almost-smile.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The conker rests on the hollow floor behind Bo’s next choice, while Bo’s tail has softened.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn the doorway from test into shared movement while preserving the ache.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Keen offers a walk for fresh air; Bo’s smile grows enough to agree, his tail picks up the bag, and Bo walks out with Keen, leaving the conker behind.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Bo chooses one small step with a witness, not a solved life.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold the room-door relationship as both move toward the same opening, then let the conker remain visible in the warm interior foreground.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo and Keen are moving through the doorway together, with the conker left behind inside.

coverage.purpose: Reset tension into a gentle laugh by making Keen the object of the comparison.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Shared threshold view angled so Keen’s turn and Bo’s watchful reaction both read without becoming a safe two-shot pattern.
coverage.storyAction: Keen says, “Mine does nothing. Watch,” turns, wiggles, and his tail hangs still; he adds, “See? Nothing.”
coverage.performanceFocus: Keen’s silliness is offered softly; Bo watches for whether this is kindness or another risk.
coverage.landingImage: Keen finished with the harmless demonstration while Bo remains present enough to look.
coverage.cutReason: New comic mechanism: from awe at Bo’s tail to Keen’s self-joke.

coverage.purpose: Make Bo’s release physical and clarify the conker payoff.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Object-aware interior view following Bo’s gaze to his tail and down to the conker as it is placed behind the choice to leave.
coverage.storyAction: Bo looks at Keen’s tail, then at his own; his tail deflates gradually, his grip loosens, and the conker comes to rest near the satchel in the warm room.
coverage.performanceFocus: The almost-smile is cautious; the conker release is not a discard with triumph, just a decision machine becoming unnecessary.
coverage.landingImage: The conker resting inside the hollow while Bo’s softened tail and small smile show one notch of ease.
coverage.cutReason: New information and motif payoff: the conker’s final placement must be unmistakable before the exit.

coverage.purpose: Land the doorway rhyme as modest shared movement.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Hold from inside the hollow with the conker visible in the warm foreground and Bo and Keen moving together toward the doorway.
coverage.storyAction: Keen suggests a walk and fresh air; Bo agrees, his tail picks up the bag, and he leaves the hollow with Keen.
coverage.performanceFocus: Bo’s agreement is a small brave exhale; his body still carries caution even as it moves.
coverage.landingImage: Bo and Keen crossing toward the outside light together, the conker left behind in the warm room.
coverage.cutReason: Final landing view; no further internal cut because the image of shared movement and abandoned decision switch is the scene’s payoff.

units.closingImage: Bo and Keen moving toward the same doorway together, the conker resting behind them inside the warm hollow near the satchel’s former place.

specificContinuityRisks: Keep Bo visibly inside the hollow at the end; he must not step through or appear ready to stride out.
The doorway must remain readable in depth as the unanswered pressure behind him.
Bo’s small paw hesitations and object focus must be legible; broad panic would invalidate the beat.
Every conker state change must be readable in relation to Bo’s paws, the satchel, and the doorway.
Bo must freeze at the threshold before the panic question; skipping the freeze removes the causal turn.
End with the conker held too tightly and the doorway still visible; do not resolve the exit.
Keen must remain at the threshold and not enter the room; his restraint is what keeps the interruption gentle.
Bo’s conker fumble must resolve into a tight hug before Keen’s explanation begins.
The startle must read as Bo’s oversize reaction, not as Keen behaving aggressively.
The tail must visibly poof twice, with the second expansion overpowering Bo’s attempt to contain it.
Keen’s awe must read as sincere before Bo softens; it cannot be played as teasing or fixing.
End with Bo only cautiously softened, not cured or proudly displaying the tail.
Keen’s tail must remain completely still during the demonstration; the joke depends on the contrast with Bo’s expressive tail.
The conker must be visibly set down and left behind inside the hollow before the exit completes.
Bo’s exit must stay modest and accompanied, not triumphant or suddenly fearless.

scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo leave the hollow oak while the tail he wants hidden remains visible and uncontrolled?

beats.sourceScript: Inside the warm hollow tree, Bo delays leaving by answering his offscreen Mum and negotiating with his conker and satchel. The room is safe, but the door already feels far away.
exactDialogue: Bo's Mum: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
Bo: I’ll go in a minute Mum.

orderedEvents.text: Warm sunlight fills a cozy hollow tree. BO, a young red squirrel, sits beside a small satchel. Next to him lies a shiny CONKER. His Mum calls to him from offscreen, we never actually see his Mum.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo's Mum
orderedEvents.text: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
Bo calls back to his Mum

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: I’ll go in a minute Mum.
(to the conker) Or forty. Forty sounds much better to me.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo's Mum
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: I’ll go in a minute Mum.

beats.whatChanges: The room shifts from simple morning safety into a delaying chamber: Mum’s offscreen prompt makes the open doorway active, and Bo answers by keeping the decision reversible through the conker and satchel.
beats.whoDrives: Bo drives the delay; Mum’s voice supplies the pressure from outside the hollow.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits to see whether Bo will actually pick up the lunch satchel and leave, while noticing that he is already treating the door as too large a step.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo stays close to manageable objects, answers Mum with a promised delay, and keeps the conker and satchel as things he can touch instead of crossing the threshold.
beats.consequence: The day has officially begun, but Bo has not moved toward it; the cosy hollow starts to feel like a loop rather than a refuge.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The beat hands into the conker decision-game: Bo has bought one minute, and the audience is primed to watch that minute stretch into a comic trap.

emotionContract.entryState: Comforted by the warm hollow and the nearby lunch satchel and conker.
emotionContract.pressure: Mum’s offscreen call, the Learning Circle, the lunch reminder and the open doorway all ask for forward motion now.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo chooses delay instead of departure, keeping the decision small enough to handle by touching objects in the room.
emotionContract.exitState: Still safe, but more trapped; the room now contains proof that he has not gone.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: His attention ricochets between conker, satchel and door; his paws hover and retract before his line promises only a minute.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience understands that the minute is not just a minute; the doorway is the real problem.

comedyContract.setup: Mum asks from outside that it is time to go and reminds him about lunch.
comedyContract.expectation: Bo will collect the satchel and leave.
comedyContract.disruption: Bo treats the nearby objects as if they can negotiate the morning for him.
comedyContract.button: His line makes delay sound tiny even as the room shows the size of what he is avoiding.
comedyContract.hold: Let the satchel, conker and open doorway share the emotional space long enough for the audience to feel how seriously Bo is outsourcing the decision.

beats.sourceScript: Bo reaches the open door and freezes, then retreats into a conker-in, conker-out loop that climbs from maybe-tomorrow to real panic. The conker becomes the physical switch for his uncertainty.
exactDialogue: Bo: Maybe, I’ll go tomorrow instead. Tomorrow sounds much better than today. Tomorrow everything will OK, not today.
Bo: Today could be OK.
Bo: What if it’s not OK?!

orderedEvents.text: He places the conker in the bag and walks towards the front door but just as he opens the door Bo freezes in place. Panic sets in.

Bo scurries back inside and takes the Conker out of his bag. Bo realizes he must go – today.

He sighs deeply and then puts the Conker back in the bag again. But his anxiety starts to rise again.
But, Today might not be OK.

beats.whatChanges: Bo’s delay becomes a visible panic loop: the door freezes him, and the conker-in/conker-out ritual starts deciding today, tomorrow and disaster for him.
beats.whoDrives: Bo drives the loop by repeatedly assigning the conker authority over his decision.
beats.audienceAnticipation: Children anticipate the conker’s next verdict; adults anticipate the moment the ritual will stop helping and start tightening around him.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo approaches the open door, freezes, retreats, then repeatedly moves the conker in and out while arguing aloud between tomorrow, today and not-OK.
beats.consequence: The conker’s tiny movement takes on giant stakes, and Bo’s body becomes less tidy with each reversal until panic breaks through the game.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The comedy of the decision switch hands into vulnerability: the room’s playful loop has made Bo easier to startle and more exposed.

emotionContract.entryState: Trying to make leaving feel manageable by reducing it to one object and one doorway.
emotionContract.pressure: The open door confronts him with the outside day, and each conker choice fails to settle the fear.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo chooses to keep restarting the decision instead of accepting any one answer.
emotionContract.exitState: Cornered by his own ritual; the panic is now louder than the cosy delay.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He freezes at the threshold, retreats, repeats the conker action, and his final line breaks the earlier negotiation rhythm.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds both the laugh of the conker loop and the ache that Bo cannot get out by deciding harder.

comedyContract.setup: Bo uses a conker as the physical switch for whether today can happen.
comedyContract.expectation: One clear conker choice will settle the argument and let him move.
comedyContract.disruption: Every choice creates the opposite choice; the more seriously Bo obeys the conker, the less control he has.
comedyContract.hold: Hold the final conker position with Bo’s panic still attached to it so the audience catches the absurd size of the job he has given the object.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: The conker, Bo’s paws, the lunch satchel and the open doorway remain readable in relation to one another so the audience tracks the decision loop and the pressure of the exit.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Each conker move has small tactile weight: paw pads gather it, set it down or pull it back; the satchel shifts only when Bo actually touches or bumps it, proving the room is responding to his fussy momentum.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A repeated in-out pattern tightens into faster, less tidy reversals until Bo’s body freezes and the final line pops out as the ritual fails him.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the conker into a magical chooser or animated character.
Do not make the loop so fast that the audience loses where the doorway is.
Do not cut away from the conker’s final position before Bo’s panic lands.

beats.sourceScript: Keen appears at the doorway with a friendly knock, startling Bo so hard the conker flies. Bo’s private loop is suddenly witnessed, but Keen’s entrance is gentle rather than invasive.

emotionContract.observableEvidence: The conker flies from Bo’s startle, while Keen stays at the doorway with simple, friendly lines rather than pushing deeper into the room.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds the relief that Keen is gentle and the tension that Bo’s real fear is about to surface.

beats.whatChanges: The real fear becomes visible: Bo names the worry that nobody will like him, the tail does the thing, and Keen’s wonder changes the tail from disaster to amazement for one fragile moment.
beats.whoDrives: Bo drives the exposure by blurting the fear; the tail forces the truth into view; Keen drives the emotional turn by answering with awe.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience inhales, waiting to see whether Keen will flinch, laugh at Bo, or make the feared tail feel unsafe.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo asks the tail to be normal when it acts out; Keen stays present, looks with delighted sincerity and names the tail as amazing.
beats.consequence: Bo does not disappear into shame; his question back to Keen shows curiosity entering the space where panic had been.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The gasp of exposure hands into a gentle opening: Bo is still embarrassed, but Keen’s response gives him enough safety to listen.

emotionContract.entryState: Socially exposed and trying to explain why the Learning Circle feels impossible.
emotionContract.pressure: His feared tail behaviour happens immediately in front of the new witness.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo stays present long enough to hear Keen’s wonder instead of fully hiding or ending the encounter.
emotionContract.exitState: Unsure but newly curious; the tail may not only be a problem if someone can see it with delight.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: Bo blurts the fear, pleads with his tail, then softens into the small, disbelieving question after Keen’s line.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: Keen’s awe remains in the room as a new possible meaning for the tail, but Bo’s fear is still visible.

comedyContract.setup: Bo fears his tail will do the thing where others can see it.
comedyContract.expectation: The tail’s action will confirm disaster and make Bo the joke.
comedyContract.disruption: The tail does act out, but Keen receives it as amazing rather than ridiculous.
comedyContract.hold: Hold briefly after Keen’s awe so Bo’s shame has time to become curiosity; do not rush into the next gag.

beats.sourceScript: Keen offers his own useless tail as a silly comparison, making himself the joke so Bo does not have to be. Bo’s tail softens, his smile grows, and the two leave together.
exactDialogue: Keen: 16	Mine does nothing. Watch.
Keen: 17	See? Nothing.
Keen: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
Bo: That does sound nice.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: 16	Mine does nothing. Watch.
Keen turns around and wiggles. His tail hangs there. Completely still.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: 17	See? Nothing.
Bo looks at Keen's tail. Then at his own. His tail slowly deflates. He almost smiles.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
BO’s smile grows to a full smile.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: That does sound nice.
His tail deflates, picks up his bag and walks out the door with Keen.

beats.whatChanges: Keen turns himself into the safe silly object, Bo’s tail softens, and the doorway becomes a shared path rather than a test.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives the release by demonstrating his own tail doing nothing and offering a walk; Bo drives the final change by accepting the step.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits for Bo to either retreat back into the room or accept Keen’s low-pressure invitation toward the outside.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen shows his tail’s uselessness without demanding Bo change, then suggests fresh air; Bo lets the smile grow and agrees.
beats.consequence: Bo and Keen move toward the doorway together, leaving the conker behind in the warm room as the decision machine loses its job.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The relief-laugh hands to forward warmth: Bo is not cured, but he is no longer alone at the threshold.

emotionContract.pressure: The doorway and Learning Circle remain ahead, and Bo must choose whether to stay inside or move with Keen.

emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The conker remains behind as a trace of the old loop, while Bo carries a small brave exhale into the next scene.

comedyContract.mechanism: Hiding failure turned into generous self-joke
comedyContract.setup: Bo’s tail has just been treated as amazing, but Bo is still unsure what to do with being seen.
comedyContract.expectation: Keen might explain, reassure too much, or make Bo’s tail the continued focus.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn the hollow oak from cosy safety into the first little delaying chamber.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Introduce Bo’s delay and make the hollow oak an active participant in the argument about leaving.

storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Recognition of avoidance disguised as routine.

storyIntent.innerAction: He shrinks the day down to touchable objects so he does not have to face the doorway yet.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play control failing quietly: reach, reconsider, answer politely, then retreat attention to the conker.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo sits compactly beside the satchel and conker, paws hovering as if one touch could settle the morning. The offscreen household prompt makes him glance toward the doorway, but his body answers by shrinking back toward the controllable objects; after speaking, he re-centers on the conker like it is safer than the threshold.
shots.animationTiming: Keep the movements small and separated by tiny hesitations: glance, paw hover, retraction, object focus. Let the doorway pressure register in stillness rather than broad alarm.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo tries to keep departure reversible by making the room’s smallest objects feel more reachable than the open threshold.

phases.observableAction: Warm hollow surfaces hold Bo close while the bright open doorway remains visible behind him as a vertical interruption.
Bo’s paws hover near the satchel, pull back, and return toward the conker as his eyeline flicks from object to doorway and back.
After the offscreen prompt, Bo keeps his body low and tidy instead of rising toward the threshold.
Bo remains beside the satchel and conker, angled inward, with the open doorway still unanswered behind him.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The offscreen household call makes the doorway active; Bo’s eyeline checks it, but his hands choose the satchel and conker, so his body stays inside and the threshold remains uncrossed.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo shifts from resting in a safe room to using the room’s objects to delay movement.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo must end visibly inside the hollow, close to the conker and satchel, with the doorway still waiting in depth.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Allow variation in blink cadence, paw tremble, tail settling, and the exact size of each hesitation, as long as Bo never appears ready to stride out.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo is a warm, nimble young squirrel whose worry shows through quick paws, small pauses, and an expressive tail.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants to keep the morning small enough to handle by staying near his satchel and conker.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: Under the offscreen prompt, he gets tidier and smaller, touching or almost touching objects instead of crossing space.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Paws close to chest, quick eyeline ricochet, compact posture, tail contained within the room’s curve.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would lean toward the opening and gather nerve through forward motion; Bo’s squirrel-specific delay is a retreat into small reachable objects.

stagePlan.purpose: Make the doorway too large for Bo’s current courage.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo places the conker in the bag and reaches the open door, but the threshold freezes him and sends him back toward tomorrow.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The first real attempt to leave collapses into retreat.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to the threshold already looming in the frame, then let the camera stop with Bo when his body stops.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo is frozen at the open door, unable to step through.

stagePlan.purpose: Convert retreat into the conker decision-game.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo scurries back inside, takes the conker out, then talks himself toward today and puts it back into the bag.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: A tiny hopeful verdict appears: today could be manageable.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Follow the conker’s path back from the bag to Bo’s paws and back again, keeping the doorway in relation so the audience tracks the loop.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The conker is back in the bag and Bo has briefly recommitted to today.

stagePlan.purpose: Let the game turn into a panic machine.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo’s anxiety rises again, he pulls the conker out once more, and the final question bursts through the ritual.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The joke of the switch flips into vulnerability; deciding harder makes him less in control.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Tighten around Bo, conker, satchel, and doorway without losing geography, ending on the conker held too tightly.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo clutches the conker with visible panic, the satchel and doorway still unresolved.

internalShotPlan.storyAction: Bo puts the conker in the bag, approaches the open door, opens it, freezes, and begins bargaining for tomorrow.

internalShotPlan.landingImage: Bo stopped at the open doorway with the bag near him and no step taken outside.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: Changed emotional state and scale of pressure: the doorway is no longer background, it is the obstacle.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Make the conker physically operate as the decision switch.

internalShotPlan.cutReason: New visual idea: the argument transfers from doorway to object loop.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Let the loop fail and expose the panic underneath.

shots.purpose: Escalate the conker from comfort object to comic decision machine, then let the machine trap Bo.
shots.audienceExperience: Children play the in-out suspense of the conker; adults feel the exhausting loop of rehearsed courage turning against itself.
shots.openingImage: Bo’s paw sets the conker into the satchel while the open doorway waits just ahead.
shots.principalPerformance: Bo must never become broadly frantic too early; the comedy comes from treating each conker placement with grave seriousness until the ritual cannot contain him.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera behaves like worry: it approaches the door, recoils into the object loop, then tightens as the loop stops helping.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: Bo moves from possible departure to repeated reversal, ending more trapped than at the start.
shots.closingImage: Bo holds the conker close against himself, with the satchel open and the doorway still visible beyond.
shots.transitionReason: A cut is stronger than staying continuous because Keen’s knock changes the scene from private ritual to witnessed exposure. If the camera simply waited through the doorway, the shock of another presence entering Bo’s sealed loop would soften.
shots.providerBoundaryExplanation: This unit’s natural 25 seconds plus the next unit’s natural 13 seconds would exceed 30 seconds; Keen’s arrival also needs a fresh first frame organized around the doorway interruption rather than the conker loop.

cinematographyContract.storyPointOfView: Bo’s worry as it tries to turn a giant social fear into a small repeatable object action.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceStart: Close but still able to see the path to the door.
cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceEnd: Tighter and more cornered, sharing Bo’s inability to find a stable verdict.
cinematographyContract.revealStrategy: Reveal panic through failed repetitions before naming the deeper fear.
cinematographyContract.shotScale: Starts as a body-and-threshold medium, compresses into object-and-hands intimacy.
cinematographyContract.lensIntent: Keep the conker tactile and important without making it magical; maintain enough depth for the door to remain the true pressure.
cinematographyContract.cameraHeight: Low at Bo’s hand and satchel height, rising only slightly when the doorway freezes him.
cinematographyContract.composition: The frame loops between three anchors: conker, satchel, doorway; each return feels less cosy and more trapped.
cinematographyContract.depthStrategy: Use depth as a treadmill: every conker move relates back to the same unresolved doorway behind or ahead.
cinematographyContract.cameraBehavior: Pursues Bo to the threshold, retreats with him, then lingers on the repeated object path until the pattern breaks.
cinematographyContract.focusStrategy: Focus follows the decision object when it changes state, then returns to Bo’s grip when the object no longer settles him.
cinematographyContract.lightingFunction: Doorway light remains constant; the emotional change comes from Bo’s changing distance to it.
cinematographyContract.paletteFunction: Warm interior holds, but tighter framing lets the brighter doorway feel more intrusive.
cinematographyContract.performanceVisibility: Hands, shoulders, breath, and the precise conker state must be readable at every reversal.
cinematographyContract.editorialPurpose: Build the comic meter of decision and reversal until the audience feels the ritual fail.
cinematographyContract.memorableLandingImage: The conker clutched like a giant answer it cannot provide.
cinematographyContract.providerInstruction: Track the conker’s in-out-in-out journey between Bo’s paws and the satchel while keeping the open doorway spatially present; let the frame tighten only as Bo’s tidy decision ritual breaks into panic.

performanceBudget.rationale: Three dialogue turns, four conker state changes, a threshold freeze, and a panic landing need the full unit but remain one causal loop under 30 seconds.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Show Bo’s delay escalating into a self-tightening panic ritual.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Suspenseful fun: which way will the conker decide?
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Empathy for a child trapped by the need to make the perfect decision.
storyIntent.outerAction: Bo approaches the door, freezes, retreats, and repeatedly moves the conker in and out of the satchel.
storyIntent.innerAction: He tries to outsource courage to a tiny object because accepting uncertainty feels too big.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play each reversal as sincere logic in Bo’s head, not random fussing; the panic arrives because the logic keeps failing.
storyIntent.mutedRead: The conker’s repeated state changes and Bo’s freeze at the doorway clearly show a decision loop becoming distress.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The doorway keeps its position as the unfinished step; the satchel waits as proof he should already be leaving.
storyIntent.soundStory: Conker taps, satchel rustles, a held breath at the threshold, then the final line breaking the rhythm.
storyIntent.motifUse: The conker is now fully the decision switch: in means today, out means retreat, neither works.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: Bo changes from believing one more conker choice can settle him to realising no choice has made today safe; cut when an outside witness is about to break the private system.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo’s panic is real even though the conker loop is funny.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: The audience still does not fully know that the tail is the specific social fear.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Bo’s reaction to the threshold changes the meaning of the door from exit to test.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Bo is alone; the absent world presses through the open door rather than through another body.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: The conker briefly holds pretend authority because Bo grants it authority.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: Bo touches the conker repeatedly and avoids stepping through the doorway.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: His eyeline should keep betraying the true problem by returning to the door after each object choice.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: A small body circling between a low object and a tall opening, then tightening around the object.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the freeze at the threshold and the tiny pause before the final panic question.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: If score is present, let it pulse lightly with the conker loop and thin out before the final panic, never covering the object sounds.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo places the conker with careful seriousness and makes his first real approach to the open door, but his momentum stops at the threshold. He scurries back into the room and turns the conker into a repeated in-and-out ritual: each placement is precise at first, then faster, less tidy, and finally a tight clutch against his chest.
shots.animationTiming: Start with measured, sincere object handling; hold the threshold freeze long enough for breath to catch. The conker loop should accelerate by commitment, not speed alone, ending with a squeezed hold and a broken rhythm.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo tries to force certainty out of one repeatable object action, but every result sends him back into another reversal.

phases.observableAction: Bo sets the conker into the satchel, gathers himself, and moves toward the open doorway with careful, contained steps.
At the threshold Bo locks in place, then retreats and repeatedly transfers the conker between his paws and the satchel.
Each reversal leaves his shoulders higher, paws less neat, and grip tighter around the conker.
Bo ends clutching the conker close, with the satchel open and the doorway still visible beyond him.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The threshold stops Bo’s forward motion; retreat puts him back at the satchel, where each conker placement or removal creates the next opposite action until the object is gripped rather than placed.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: A tidy departure attempt becomes a self-tightening object loop, then breaks into visible distress.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo must finish with the conker held too tightly against himself, the satchel unresolved, and the doorway still spatially clear.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: The exact path of the scurry, number of tiny paw adjustments, tail counterbalance, and breath pattern may vary, but the conker state changes must remain unmistakable.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s worry and curiosity pull him into quick, sincere, object-focused behaviour; his tail and paws reveal what he cannot settle.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants the conker to make the outside step feel decided and safe.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: When the doorway confronts him, he freezes, retreats, and overcommits to the repeated object action.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Light squirrel steps, abrupt stop, paws gathering the conker carefully at first and clutching it by the end, tail balancing each reversal.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen under pressure would show a gulp and step through; Bo uniquely turns pressure into a fussy decision ritual around his satchel and conker.

comedyStaging.staysVisible: The conker, Bo’s paws, the lunch satchel and the open doorway remain readable in relation to one another so the audience tracks the decision loop and the pressure of the exit.
comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: Each conker move has small tactile weight: paw pads gather it, set it down or pull it back; the satchel shifts only when Bo actually touches or bumps it, proving the room is responding to his fussy momentum.
comedyStaging.payoffShape: A repeated in-out pattern tightens into faster, less tidy reversals until Bo’s body freezes and the final line pops out as the ritual fails him.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the conker into a magical chooser or animated character.
Do not make the loop so fast that the audience loses where the doorway is.
Do not cut away from the conker’s final position before Bo’s panic lands.

storyIntent.environmentPressure: The doorway becomes embodied by Keen, turning abstract outside pressure into a relationship possibility.
storyIntent.soundStory: The knock should be playful but soft; the conker fumble supplies the comic texture; Keen’s voice lowers the room’s alarm.

shots.physicalPerformance: Keen appears as a soft presence at the doorway: he taps lightly, peeks in, and keeps his weight outside the room’s center. Bo jolts before he can compose himself; the conker pops free, bounces through several fumbled catches, and ends hugged tight as Bo checks the object and then Keen.
shots.animationTiming: Let the knock breathe before Keen fully reads. Bo’s startle should be quick and springy, followed by a comic fumble with clear catches and slips, then a gentle settle that proves Keen is not advancing.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Keen offers entry as gently as possible; Bo’s body reveals how sealed and overwound the private loop has become.

phases.observableAction: Keen holds at the threshold, taps softly on the hollow, and peeks in without crossing into the room.
Bo jumps, launching the conker upward, then fumbles it through several catches before trapping it against his body.
Bo’s eyes snap from the hugged conker to Keen, measuring the object loss and the new witness in one quick check.
Keen remains calmly at the doorway with soft posture and no forward step after Bo’s startle.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s soft doorway knock interrupts the private loop; Bo’s startle sends the conker into the air, forcing a messy recovery, and Keen’s stillness prevents the interruption from becoming a chase into the room.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo’s private control becomes witnessed exposure, but Keen’s body language keeps the encounter gentle.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo must end hugging the conker inside the hollow while Keen waits at the threshold, leaving space between them.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Allow play in the conker’s arc, Bo’s fumble pattern, and Keen’s micro-softening, provided the startle is Bo’s oversize response and Keen does not crowd him.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Keen is forward and curious, but real courage for him includes softness before action rather than fearless pushing.
characterTruths.playableWant: Keen wants to make contact without startling the room more than necessary.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: At the threshold, he reduces his usual momentum into a light knock, a small lean, and a patient wait.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Forward interest contained in soft knees, open chest, gentle peek, and no uninvited step inside.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Bo would retreat into objects at this doorway; Keen uniquely brings brave curiosity while choosing restraint.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s squirrel body reacts fast; worry shows before he can tidy it into words.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants to recover the conker and regain a little control in front of the newcomer.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He springs, fumbles, then protects the object against his chest.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Quick vertical jolt, nimble but messy paw catches, tight hug of the conker, rapid eyeline from object to visitor.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would likely convert the mishap into forward engagement; Bo’s specific response is to clutch the decision object and stay deeper inside.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo’s words spill faster than his body can manage: he clutches near the conker, then turns inward as his tail suddenly expands and takes over the room. He grabs at it, trying to compress it back down, but the second expansion defeats the tidy effort. Keen stays still and openly impressed; Bo’s grip loosens, his shoulders drop, and he looks back with cautious disbelief rather than immediate confidence.
shots.animationTiming: Protect the spill, then make each tail expansion feel like a soft physical burst with follow-through in Bo’s balance. Hold Keen’s still reaction long enough to redirect the room, then let Bo’s release arrive slowly.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo expects visible difference to cost him safety; Keen’s sincere stillness gives that visible difference a new possible meaning.

phases.observableAction: Bo leans forward with the conker close, paws tight and speech-driven motion spilling out faster than his posture can organize.
Bo’s tail expands suddenly; he grabs it with both paws, tries to hold it down, and is pulled off balance when it expands again.
Keen looks directly at the enlarged tail with widened eyes, lifted face, and still body, showing delight rather than alarm.
Bo stops fighting as hard, loosens his grip on the tail, lowers his shoulders, and checks Keen’s face with a small uncertain look.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Bo’s body tightens around the exposed worry; the tail expands beyond his hands, forcing the frame and his balance wider, and Keen’s still delighted gaze interrupts Bo’s attempt to hide it.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: The enlarged tail changes from something Bo is wrestling to something he cautiously allows to be seen.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo must end beside the enlarged tail with a softened grip and a questioning look toward Keen, not fully cured or hidden.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: The tail’s exact bounce, Bo’s paw placement, and Keen’s facial micro-reaction may vary, but the second expansion must clearly overpower Bo’s control and Keen must read sincere before Bo softens.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Bo’s large fluffy tail is an emotional and movement anchor; under worry, paws pull close and the tail tells the truth bigger than his face.
characterTruths.playableWant: Bo wants to make his tail small and socially manageable in front of the witness.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He pleads physically with the tail by grabbing, squeezing, and trying to contain it, then pauses when the witness does not recoil.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Tight paws on tail fur, off-balance squirrel posture, shoulders lifted then dropping, eyeline checking Keen before trusting the moment.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen’s pressure tell is a gulp before a step; Bo’s canon tail makes the feeling physically larger than his control, so another character could not carry this beat.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Keen’s courage is bright, curious, and relationship-forward, with action guided by visible feeling rather than swagger.
characterTruths.playableWant: Keen wants Bo to know the tail can be looked at with delight, without turning Bo into a target.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He holds still instead of charging in, letting his impressed gaze arrive before any movement toward Bo.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Open face, widened eyes, lifted chin, body quiet at the threshold, no grab for the tail and no laugh at Bo.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: A deadpan or fixer character could make the tail a joke or a problem; Keen uniquely reframes it through eager, sincere wonder.

stagePlan.purpose: Release the held vulnerability through Keen making himself the safe silly object.

stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The joke moves away from Bo; Keen chooses harmless self-exposure.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to a threshold-shared setup that treats Keen’s demonstration as generous silliness, not a performance demanding applause.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Keen has demonstrated a tail that does nothing, with Bo watching rather than hiding.

stagePlan.purpose: Make Bo’s old decision machine visibly lose its job.

stagePlan.observableEndState: The conker rests on the hollow floor behind Bo’s next choice, while Bo’s tail has softened.

stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Bo chooses one small step with a witness, not a solved life.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold the room-door relationship as both move toward the same opening, then let the conker remain visible in the warm interior foreground.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo and Keen are moving through the doorway together, with the conker left behind inside.

shots.purpose: Release the tension with Keen’s generous self-joke, then land Bo’s first small outward step without curing the fear.

shots.openingImage: Keen at the threshold turned slightly toward Bo, ready to make his own tail the demonstration.
